item.title: Denmark accuses Russia of assassination plot, expels diplomat
item.description: Denmark has accused Moscow of being behind a failed assassination attempt targeting a Ukrainian-American rapper in Copenhagen, further escalating tensions between Europe and Russia. In response, Danish authorities have ordered the expulsion of a Russian diplomat and announced tighter restrictions on visas for Russian tourists. Yuka Royer reports.

item.title: Houthis launch strikes on Saudi Arabia
item.description: Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen continue to exchange strikes with the Saudi-led coalition. The coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles fired towards Riyadh early on Saturday. It marks the second Houthi attack on the Saudi capital in recent days, following Saudi-led strikes on Houthi targets in Yemen. Yuka Royer has the latest.

item.title: ECB seeks industry partners for tokenized deposits, securities experiments
item.description: Industry groups have until Dec. 11 to apply for the ECB’s first experimental exercises under its Appia initiative, with later submissions reviewed on a rolling basis.

item.title: Russian projectiles hit Poland as NATO tensions rise
item.description: Three Russian projectiles came down in Poland on Friday, prompting NATO to condemn what it called a grave violation of Polish airspace. A suspected jet-powered drone and a missile struck separate locations near the Ukrainian border, while another missile crashed just 35 kilometres from an area where European troops are taking part in military exercises. Meanwhile, troops from eight NATO countries are conducting drills in neighbouring Lithuania. With US-led peace talks yet to make a breakthrough, tensions between Europe and Russia remain high. Peter O’Brien reports.

item.title: Nations League: France to face Spain in quarter-finals, England to take on Norway
item.description: A chance for revenge. Beaten by Spain in the World Cup semi-finals last July, France will meet La Roja again in the Nations League quarter-finals next March.

item.title: 2027 Politics Watch: From two ADC court rulings to Obi’s 10,000MW pledge
item.description: A federal judge refused to let Atiku Abubakar and the ADC amend their challenge to Bola Tinubu’s eligibility. In a separate judgment, the court ordered the ADC to restore Omar Suleiman’s Adamawa nomination. Peter Obi set targets for power, healthcare and education in Onitsha, and opposition parties moved their summit to 30 November. The post 2027 Politics Watch: From two ADC court rulings to Obi’s 10,000MW pledge appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .

item.title: 🚨 Who saw this coming in the summer: Bundesliga boss extends deal early!
item.description: 🚨 Who saw this coming in the summer: Bundesliga boss extends deal early! Daniel Thioune is staying at Werder Bremen! As the Green-Whites announced on Saturday morning, the head coach has signed an early extension to his contract, which was due to expire at the end of the season. "We have complete faith in Daniel's work. Despite a difficult situation, his meticulous approach helped him achieve the target we set last season, and he has visibly strengthened and developed the team this season," explained managing director Clemens Fritz. Indeed, a day before the eagerly awaited northern derby against HSV, the team are sitting in a sensational sixth place. That was hardly on the cards just a few weeks ago. Bremen endured a largely difficult summer transfer window, and there were doubts about Thioune too. But the numerous last-minute signings have been a resounding success, and the coach has also shown that he can turn the players at his disposal into a cohesive side that plays attractive, attacking football. "I'm really enjoying the opportunity to work with this team at Werder. We have some great characters in this group, and we're getting better and better at putting our footballing ideas into practice," Thioune fittingly explained. "I'm very grateful for the trust the club's leadership has placed in me, and I'm looking forward to the future at this cool club." This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇩🇪 here.

item.title: EU, UK reach reset deal after Brexit
item.description: The UK and the EU signed three agreements on Friday at a summit in Brussels, marking a new effort to reset post-Brexit relations. The deals aim to reduce red tape for food exports, link emissions trading schemes and allow tens of thousands of young people to live and work more freely across the Channel. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called Brexit an “obvious failure” to deliver on its promises and wants to deepen ties with the EU, a position criticised by veteran Brexiteer Nigel Farage, who has warned of a political backlash. Daniel Quinlan has this story.

item.title: PCB central contracts 2026-27 full list: Mohammad Rizwan, Shan Masood, and Saim Ayub dropped; Babar Azam excluded from T20I deal
item.description: PCB central contracts 2026-27 full list: Mohammad Rizwan, Shan Masood, and Saim Ayub dropped; Babar Azam excluded from T20I deal originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Pakistan’s board has unveiled its new central contracts after a long delay. Several well-known names, including Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood, have been left off the list. A fresh format-based structure means no player holds a deal across all three formats. MORE: PAK WK Ghazi Ghori's admission leaves cricket world stunned amid Sandpapergate End of the road in T20Is for Babar Azam? PCB snubs Test skipper from T20I contract A number of familiar faces have disappeared from Pakistan’s central contracts list for 2026-27, and the biggest surprises are former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood. Opener Imam-ul-Haq has also been left out of the list that the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) released on Saturday. The announcement arrived much later than usual, since the previous set of contracts had run out on June 30. The wait ended with a revamped system, and the changes are bigger than most expected. Test skipper Babar Azam has no T20I contract this time. The batsman has often been under the scanner for his low strike rates in T20s and the recent contract list is another hammer blow to his T20I future. MORE: ‘I thought I was playing against 22 guys’: Shoaib recalls Pakistan's match-fixing crisis PCB central contracts 2026-27: How the new format-based system works Under the new structure, players are placed in categories linked to the formats they are expected to play, rather than in the old ranked grades. Test captain Babar and Salman Ali Agha are the only two players handed a Test and ODI deal. ODI captain Shaheen Shah Afridi sits in the ODI/T20 category, while Sahibzada Farhan, who led Pakistan in their most recent T20 Internationals, has a deal in the T20 group alone. No player has been offered a contract that covers all three formats. The board did not reveal how much each category will pay. It did hand contracts to 38 players, and most of them have landed in a newly created development category. MORE: IND vs PAK in Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026: Start time, date, venue and how to watch (getty) Who are the notable absentees from PCB central contracts 2026-27? Rizwan’s absence is the most notable of all. The wicketkeeper held a Category B deal last year, but he has been caught up in off-field controversies and was sent home midway through the Test tour of England. Few were shocked by the decisions on Shan and Imam, given what has happened lately. Shan was recently replaced as Test captain, while Imam and Rizwan were both sent back from England, where Pakistan were whitewashed in a three-match series. Shadab Khan, another senior player and former captain, has been placed only in the T20 category. The others missing are Abdullah Shafique, Mohammad Haris, Mohammad Nawaz, Noman Ali, Hussain Talat, Khurram Shahzad, Khu

item.title: Seville’s Passionate ‘Gran Derbi’ Divides A City Looking To The Future
item.description: Pablo Fornals of Real Betis celebrates a goal against Sevilla at the Pizjuán last November. Europa Press via Getty Images The last time Real Betis visited Sevilla’s Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán for ‘ El Gran Derbi ’, the game was stopped for more than 15 minutes. Betis won 2-0 that afternoon in November 2025, with second-half goals from Pablo Fornals and Sergi Altimira. Sevilla striker Isaac Romero was sent off and objects thrown from the stands forced the referee to halt play. On Saturday evening, at 6:30pm local time, the Seville derby goes back to Nervión. It is the 13th round of LaLiga, but in Seville nobody treats it as one game among 38. “Here in Seville, football is a way of life, like a religion,” Álvaro Valles told me in a LALIGA press event this week. The Betis goalkeeper was born just outside the city and came through the club’s academy. A rivalry older than LaLiga Sevilla were founded in 1890 while Betis came later, out of a split at Sevilla, and in 1914 a merger created Real Betis Balompié. The first Seville derby was played on October 8, 1915, and Sevilla won it 4-3, and the two side have now met 145 times in official competition. Sevilla lead the record with 66 wins, but have failed to win any of the last three. After November’s heated affair, the return game at La Cartuja in March finished 2-2, after Betis led 2-0 at half time and Alexis Sánchez and Isaac Romero brought Sevilla level. “More than three points” What sets the derby apart is that both clubs carry national weight from the same city. “These are two powerful clubs at national level, and the rivalry is huge,” Valles told international media. “Having two nationally important clubs in the city of Seville makes this match very important all over the world.” Alvaro Valles of Real Betis gestures during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Betis Balompie at BVB Stadion Dortmund. Getty Images Valles has a useful comparison, as Betis are in the Champions League this season, and he has already played at Borussia Dortmund, with a trip to Bayern Munich to come in January. Asked how those atmospheres compare with a Seville derby, he said they are not alike. “A derby is a one-off game. I always say it doesn’t matter what form either team is in. It’s like a final,” he says. “They’re still worth three points like any other game, but against your eternal rival they’re more than three points. It’s the pride of a whole city.” He has lived the rivalry since childhood as Valles grew up in La Rinconada, left the Betis academy to make his name at UD Las Palmas, and came back to the club in 2025 after spending a year in the stands to see out his contract and ensure a move back to his boyhood club. He calls the return “a dream I had wanted to fulfil since I was a kid: playing at home, in my city, for the club of my life.” Two homes in flux The stadiums that built this rivalry are both about to change. Betis have not played at the Benito Villamarín

item.title: Manchester United rival Liverpool for Italy international defender as club also informed of former midfielder's potential 2027 return
item.description: Atalanta BC v Parma Calcio - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United are rivalling Liverpool for Italy international centre-back Giorgio Scalvini as they plan for life after Lisandro Martinez. The Old Trafford hierarchy have also been alerted to a possible 2027 reunion with former midfielder Scott McTominay amid contract talks at Napoli. Recruitment chiefs scout defensive targets According to TEAMtalk , United are carrying out detailed scouting work on Scalvini as they prepare to reinforce up front, at left-back and in central defence. The Italian has caught the eye of several recruitment departments and could become a major defensive target in 2027, either in January or next summer. That search comes as Martinez enters the final months of his deal, despite a one-year club option. Agent chief questions Barcelona interest Speculation surrounding Martinez's future has gathered pace following earlier claims from the outlet that Barcelona admire the Argentine defender, alongside reports in Spain suggesting he is open to listening to an offer from the Liga giants. However, the president of the Spanish Association of Football Agents, Pedro Bravo, has poured cold water on any potential switch to Catalonia. Addressing the transfer rumours, Bravo said: "Lisandro, as far as I'm aware, neither Deco nor [Hansi] Flick are keen on him." He added that the message coming from Flick and sporting director Deco regarding Martinez is clear: "He's a good player, but we don't like him. He doesn't fit in with us." Regardless of Barcelona's stance, Martinez's contract situation still points towards an Old Trafford exit in the near future. Scottish playmaker considers English comeback Alongside their defensive planning, the report states that former United midfielder McTominay is seriously weighing up a return to the Premier League in 2027. His previous employers have already been notified of the opportunity to bring the academy graduate back to Manchester, and club officials have not dismissed the prospect. The publication's sources believe Napoli remain hopeful of keeping the Scotland international in Serie A, with his current agreement set to expire in 18 months. Because the two parties are currently far apart in contract negotiations, intermediaries have begun pushing him towards potential landing spots in case no middle ground can be found. Injury recovery dictates winter timing Timing will play a decisive role in how United approach both pursuits over the coming months. Because Scalvini has only recently returned from injury, a January move may arrive too soon, meaning United and Liverpool will keep tracking his form before deciding when to bid. Meanwhile, McTominay's ongoing standoff in Italy will determine whether a 2027 reunion becomes a concrete option.

item.title: Cleworth set for 200th Wrexham game
item.description: Defender Max Cleworth has scored 11 league goals in total for Wrexham [Getty Images] Max Cleworth is set to reach another milestone in his Wrexham career this weekend – and the defender is still only 24. A product of Wrexham's academy, Cleworth will make his 200th appearance in all competitions for the club if he features against Lincoln City in the Championship on Saturday (15:00 GMT). "I found out a bit recently that it was coming up," Cleworth said. "It's something I won't think about until maybe after the game and just try and focus on putting in another good performance and another good team performance hopefully. "it's a very proud moment to come through the academy and end up getting 200 games. It's something that, as I said, I'm proud of." Cleworth has played a key role in each of Wrexham's three successive promotions - rising from the National League to the Championship. He made his league debut in manager Phil Parkinson's first game at the helm in August 2021, at Solihull Moors. "That's a game that I look back on with really good memories," Cleworth said. "Obviously, it was the first pre-season of the gaffer's [Parkinson] and then I played a few games in pre-season. "That week's training, I was in and out of the back three. The day before, I was in the set-up team. "That was it really, I told my dad not to bother coming in. I went and played, it was 2-2 in the end." Parkinson cautious on Wrexham trio injury return Injuries, noise & scalps - Wrexham's season so far A shock departure and key results - inside Wrexham's seismic week Cleworth's progress is often used as a marker of the huge strides Wrexham have made under Parkinson and the Hollywood ownership of the club. But Cleworth's first-team debut came before Parkinson's arrival and a whole year prior to Rob Mac and Ryan Reynolds announcing they wanted to buy the club. "I think naturally my debut is one that I'll never be able to forget – Ayr United at home," said Cleworth, recalling the Scottish Challenge Cup tie in September 2019. "Colchester was my first goal in the league. I think it was Gloucester at home in the FA Trophy was my first actual goal, so that one will always stick out. "It's nice to look back on, but hopefully we can make some more memories as we move forward." Having given him his league debut only days after he had turned 19, Parkinson has seen Cleworth develop into one of the club's key players. "It's an amazing story," said Parkinson. "Because for Maxi to be a key figure in all the divisions, it's great. It's great for him and for his family to have watched that. "Even today, Maxi's one of the last off the training pitch, working on key elements of his game, and that's a great message for all our academy players. "Max Cleworth's development has come with working a lot of departments, tactical understanding of the levels and physical improvement in the gym. "Also dealing with the ups and downs of football because there were times when, as a young player we left him

item.title: Stephen A. Smith says there’s one rule stopping him from running for President
item.description: Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Sports analyst Stephen A. Smith gives an update on whether he will try to become the next US President. Over the years, Stephen A. Smith has built an impressive fan following thanks to his unfiltered takes on the NBA and NFL. So much so that Smith has now expanded his coverage to things outside of sports, including politics in the United States of America. There have been times when the ESPN analyst has contemplated running for president, but Smith has seemingly given up on that dream. Stephen A. Smith explains why he will not run for US President During a recent podcast appearance with NBA legend Kevin Garnett, Smith talked about a plethora of things. Soon, the conversation shifted to if the ESPN on-air talent wants to run for president. Well, Smith has shut the door on any possibility and it’s because of one important rule. “Listen, would I give all of this up to be the President of the United States of America? Yes, I would. Would I give it up to campaign for the president? H___ no. And according to the rules, you have to give up everything. What they say is you’ve got to give up your money because, by virtue of what I do, let me tell you this: there’s something with the FCC called ‘the equal-time rule,” Smith said. He added, “And equal time means that because of what I do and because I’m on the air all the time, the minute I announce that I’m running, I have to come off the air and give up my career and the money that comes with it. “Now, that ain’t happening, dog. That’s not happening.” Running for president doesn’t automatically mean that Smith will win the election, and if he fails, he could lose relevance among fans. After all, it has taken him decades to build his audience, and even a few months’ gap could splash cold water over his years of hard work. Read more: ‘He’s done’ – Stephen A. Smith says there is no way back for Dallas Cowboys man who he simply cannot defend Stephen A. Smith says there’s something people ‘continuously forget’ about the Jacksonville Jaguars ‘Not good enough’ – Stephen A. Smith unleashes on Giants RB Cam Skattebo

item.title: New Man Utd boss Pochettino sure years in USA made him ‘better coach’
item.description: FILE PHOTO - USA coach Mauricio Pochettino reacts from the touchline during the International Friendly soccer match between USA and Germany at Soldier Field. (is associated with: «New Man Utd boss Pochettino sure years in USA made him ‘better coach’») Christian Charisius/dpa New Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino believes his time in international football with the United States has made him a better coach but admitted he missed the day-to-day feel of club management. An overnight flight from Cincinnati to Manchester took Pochettino from his post-match duties after the United States’ win over Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning to United’s Carrington complex, where he has quickly got to work ahead of Sunday’s clash with old rivals Liverpool. Pochettino has been linked with United’s top job before but, while he takes over with the club in the bottom three having won only one Premier League match all season, the 54-year-old believes he is better placed for the Old Trafford challenge now than ever before. “Of course we were missing [club football], we were missing it a lot,” he said. “I think we are animals of the grass. We like to feel the grass, we need to smell the grass and try to help the players to improve every day. “It’s true that it’s a different job when you are in the national team, but at the same time you learn a lot, and I think we are much better coaches now, much better coaches.” Pochettino has plenty of Premier League experience with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, taking Tottenham to both a Champions League and League Cup final, albeit without winning either, and was also a league winner with Paris St Germain. But the man who took the United States to the last 16 of this summer’s World Cup argued the pressure at international level is just as great as in club football. “The expectation and the pressure was massive,” he said. “I remember always in SoFi (Los Angeles), our first game against Paraguay, the pressure was massive, there were more than 200 celebrity people expecting us to win and to play well and all the country was behind us. “They say when you are in the Premier League or in LaLiga or in France, OK, you feel the pressure when you manage this type of size of club. “But being there was, I promise, it was massive pressure, but we found a way to translate that pressure into energy. And that is what we were talking about when you say we learn.” The experience of international football, where managers have only a few weeks a year to get their ideas across to players they work with in short bursts, could help Pochettino engineer a turnaround in United’s fortunes after a start to the season which has seen them win only three of 15 matches. But Pochettino played down the challenge of arriving midway through the campaign. “I think our job is to adapt and to go ahead a little bit,” he said. “The most important thing is to understand when you arrive at a new club, the culture, the history and the identity. “We

item.title: Is England v New Zealand on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch All Blacks clash
item.description: England seek back-to-back victories over New Zealand for just the second time in their history as they take on a wounded All Blacks side at Twickenham. Dave Rennie’s tourists were stunned by Wales for the first time since 1953 last Saturday, and must now look to rebound at a ground at which they were beaten last November. That success marked the high of England’s time under Steve Borthwick so far, but confidence has built again for his squad after big wins over Australia and Japan. The intensity will ratchet up significantly, though, as the All Blacks come to town on the penultimate weekend of the Nations Championship. Here’s everything you need to know. When is England vs New Zealand? England vs New Zealand is due to kick off at 2.10pm GMT on Saturday 21 November at the Allianz Stadium, Twickenham. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch the match live on ITV1, with coverage from 1pm GMT. A live stream will be available on ITVX. Team news England revert to a virtually identical matchday 23 to that which beat Australia a fortnight ago. The sole exception comes on the left wing, where Immanuel Feyi-Waboso is injured; Will Joseph retains his place after registering five tries against Japan. Six forwards are again readied on the bench, with Ben Spencer and Marcus Smith providing backline cover. England XV: 1 Fin Baxter, 2 Jamie George, 3 Joe Heyes; 4 Maro Itoje (capt.), 5 Alex Coles; 6 Ollie Chessum, 7 Ben Curry, 8 Ben Earl; 9 Jack van Poortvliet, 10 Fin Smith; 11 Will Joseph, 12 Seb Atkinson, 13 Henry Slade, 14 Tommy Freeman; 15 George Furbank. Replacements : 16 Luke Cowan-Dickie, 17 Ellis Genge, 18 Will Stuart, 19 George Martin, 20 Greg Fisilau, 21 Henry Pollock; 22 Ben Spencer, 23 Marcus Smith. The All Blacks bring back the big guns following a first defeat to Wales since 1953. Beauden Barrett becomes just the fourth player to reach 150 international caps as he retains his place at full-back, while Will Jordan and Jordie Barrett are welcome returnees from injury. Codie Taylor captains the side from hooker while Leicester Fainga’anuku provides both back row and outside back cover among the replacements. New Zealand XV: 1 Ethan de Groot, 2 Codie Taylor (capt.), 3 Fletcher Newell; 4 Scott Barrett, 5 Fabian Holland; 6 Tupou Vaa’i, 7 Peter Lakai, 8 Wallace Sititi; 9 Cam Roigard, 10 Damian McKenzie; 11 Josh Moorby, 12 Jordie Barrett, 13 Anton Lienert-Brown, 14 Will Jordan; 15 Beauden Barrett. Replacements: 16 Asafo Aumua, 17 George Bower, 18 Pasilio Tosi, 19 Anton Segner, 20 Leicester Fainga’anuku; 21 Cortez Ratima, 22 Richie Mo’unga, 23 Rieko Ioane.

item.title: Is Ireland v South Africa on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Springboks clash
item.description: At the end of a chaotic week, Ireland and South Africa collide in a Nations Championship grudge match in Dublin. Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus will be absent having received a six-match ban for comments that questioned the integrity of match officials on Monday. The two-time World Cup winning coach will be running a live stream of his reaction to what could be a feisty affair, with Ireland fly half Sam Prendergast cleared to feature following a disciplinary hearing. Ireland have sprung a selection surprise, too, with captain Dan Sheehan deployed at No 8 rather than in his usual hooking role. Here’s everything you need to know. When is Ireland vs South Africa? Ireland vs South Africa is due to kick off at 4.40pm GMT on Saturday 21 November at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch the match live on ITV1, with coverage following the conclusion of England against New Zealand. A live stream will be available via ITVX. Team news Ireland are led from No 8 by Dan Sheehan, back after concussion in a new role he did occupy recently for Leinster. Ronan Kelleher therefore starts at hooker, while Sam Prendergast is cleared to start following a disciplinary hearing for a dangerous tackle. Ireland XV: 1 Andrew Porter, 2 Ronan Kelleher, 3 Tadhg Furlong; 4 Joe McCarthy, 5 Tadhg Beirne; 6 Ryan Baird, 7 Josh van der Flier, 8 Dan Sheehan (capt.); 9Jamison Gibson-Park, 10 Sam Prendergast; 11 Mack Hansen, 12 Stuart McCloskey, 13 Robbie Henshaw, 14 Robert Baloucoune; 15 Hugo Keenan. Replacements: 16 Tom Stewart, 17 Tom O’Toole, 18 Thomas Clarkson, 19 James Ryan, 20 Nick Timoney; 21 Craig Casey, 22 Ciaran Frawley, 23 Bundee Aki. South Africa also make a switch at the base of the scrum with Jasper Wiese suspended. Cameron Hanekom wears No 8 with Eben Etzebeth a significant returnee to the pack as he closes in on 150 Springboks caps – with Franco Mostert now his partner due to a niggle that rules out Ruan Nortje. Six forwards are included on the bench, but there is no place for Manie Libbok following his crucial missed conversion in Paris. South Africa XV: 1 Ox Nche, 2 Malcolm Marx, 3 Wilco Louw; 4 Eben Etzebeth, 5 Franco Mostert; 6 Siya Kolisi (capt.), 7 Pieter-Steph du Toit, 8 Cameron Hanekom; 9 Morne van den Berg, 10 Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu; 11 Ethan Hooker, 12 Damian de Allende, 13 Jesse Kriel, 14 Kurt-Lee Arendse; 15 Damian Willemse. item.title: Is Scotland v Japan on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Nations Championship clash
item.description: Scotland will look to push for a strong Nations Championship finish as they conclude their home November efforts against Japan . Gregor Townsend’s side were far from their best against Australia yet bounced back from defeat to New Zealand with success against the Wallabies, and could yet usurp Ireland in the northern hemisphere pool table. To do that, though, will require a bonus point victory and points difference swing – eminently achievable if Japan are as poor as they were against England in their last outing. Eddie Jones will expect far better of his side in Edinburgh. Here’s everything you need to know. When is Scotland vs Japan? Scotland vs Japan is due to kick off at 2.10pm GMT on Saturday 21 November at Murrayfield. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch the match live on ITV4, with coverage from 1.30pm GMT. A live stream will be available on ITVX. Team news Gregor Townsend makes sweeping changes to his side, with injuries taking their toll. Captain Sione Tuipulotu, Ben White, Jack Dempsey, Pierre Schoeman and Scott Cummings are among those absent, while Finn Russell, Ewan Ashman and Huw Jones have been given a week off. OIlie Leatherbarrow earns a first international start having made his Scotland debut last week, and begings on the openside after a late injury for Rory Darge. Stafford McDowall is captain. Scotland XV: 1 Nathan McBeth, 2 Gregor Hiddleston, 3 Zander Fagerson; 4 Jonny Gray, 5 Max Williamson; 6 Liam McConnell, 7 Ollie Leatherbarrow, 8 Matt Fagerson; 9 Jamie Dobie, 10 Tom Jordan; 11 Kyle Rowe, 12 Rory Hutchinson, 13 Stafford McDowall (capt.), 14 Darcy Graham; 15 Ollie Smith. Replacements : 16 Seb Stephen, 17 Rory Sutherland, 18 Will Hurd, 19 Gregor Brown, 20 Magnus Bradbury, 21 Freddy Douglas; 22 George Horne, 23 Blair Kinghorn. Japan also bear a fresh look in places. Jack Cornelsen moves into the second row for the suspended Harry Hockings, with Faulua Makisi in at No 8. Ryosuke Iwaihara and Jisu Lee take the places of the absent Shuhei Takeuchi and Dyolan Riley. item.title: Cummins' integrity not compromised - CA
item.description: Pat Cummins was named Australia captain in 2021 [Getty Images] Cricket Australia has "unequivocally rejected" the suggestion that captain Pat Cummins' integrity has been compromised by the sandpaper scandal. On Saturday CA gave its "unanimous support" to Cummins, and he said he would take part in the independent forum set up for players and staff. Cummins has faced claims to step down as captain after Cameron Bancroft's detailed testimony supported claims made by Usman Khawaja that the entire Australia team knew of the plan to tamper with the ball during a Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018. CA and Cummins met this week, with the former saying it was "determined to steward Australian cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn". "We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa," CA said. "We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat's integrity has been compromised." CA chief executive Todd Greenberg said Cummins has been an "exemplary leader" in his five years as captain. "He has consistently spoken and articulated what happened back in 2018 in his version of events. Nothing's changed. Thus, nothing's changing with our captaincy," Greenberg told BBC Sport. Greenberg acknowledged that people's version of events "directly contradict" each other but said Cummins has "not moved one inch" from his story, giving the same account now as he did when interviewed the day after the Cape Town Test in 2018. Cummins is due to lead Australia in the opening match of a four-Test series against New Zealand starting on 9 December in Perth. The pace bowler reiterated his stance that he had no involvement in or knowledge of the sandpaper plot during a 68-minute news conference last week. Cummins has said he will attend the forum that has been set up by CA for players and staff to share their version of events. "I support the forum 100%. I will be there," he said. "All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say. "There will be a lot of difficult conversations, but that is what's needed. "Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority." The row over the sandpaper saga, one of the biggest controversies in Test history, has engulfed Australian sport since Khawaja's claims emerged two weeks ago. In 2018 Bancroft was banned for nine months and captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner for a year after Bancroft was caught rubbing sandpaper on the ball during the third Test at Newlands. Khawaja, who retired from international cricket this year, wrote in his autobiography that all the Australia team knew and should have taken responsibility. He has since been supported by Warner and bowler

item.title: Mika Baur’s injury presents early Celtic opportunity for Joel Van Den Berg
item.description: Mika Baur’s injury presents early Celtic opportunity for Joel Van Den Berg Martin O’Neill and the Celtic supporters have been hit with a massive blow after it was revealed that influential midfielder Mika Baur will miss up to ten weeks with an ankle ligament injury… Mika Baur ‘fouls’ Greg Kiltie of Kilmarnock (ultimately leading to Kasper Hogh’s goal being dissallowed) during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Kilmarnock at Celtic Park on November 08, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) The German international midfielder limped off in the closing stages of the 1-0 win over Kilmarnock a fortnight ago and was forced to pull out of the German under 21 squad for their recent matches. However Celtic fans were hoping that this was no more than a knock meaning that the hugely impressive Celtic star would be back in action after the International break. However that is NOT the case and instead it is going to be around February before we see Baur back in action, although the player himself has told Martin O’Neill that he is a quick healer, so maybe that estimated return date can be brought forward a week or two. Mika Baur of Celtic passes the ball during the UEFA Europa League match between Celtic FC and Besiktas JK at Celtic Park on November 05, 2026. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) In an update on Friday at his mainstream media conference , the Celtic manager somewhat relectantly broke the bad news: “It his ankle. He’ll be out for some considerable time. It’s a real shame. He was playing great for us. “I think there’s talk about 10 weeks, but I spoke to Mika yesterday and he’s a quick healer. There’s things that he can’t do for a while. His foot’s in the boot and stuff like this here. “I think it was a bigger injury than, for instance, that Joel van den Berg had, so it might be a couple of extra weeks.” Benjamin Nygren of Celtic is seen during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Kilmarnock at Celtic Park on November 08, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Benjamin Nygren is also doubtful after missing Friday’s training session due to a heel issue he picked up whilst on international duty with Sweden. With Mika out for a couple of months, and Benji looking doubtful for today’s match against St Mirren, it opens the door for aforementioned young Joel van den Berg to show what he can provide to the first team. Joël van den Berg of Celtic arrives prior to the Scottish Premiership 2026/27 match between Celtic and Aberdeen at Celtic Park on September 02, 2026 . (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Today might not be the time for the Dutch midfielder to start but we perhaps can expect to see him coming off the bench. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain will of course be able to step in as will Luke McCowan, but we will be needing others to contribute, and young van den Berg could well be one of those to do so. The 19 year old was signed for a deal believed to be worth up to £3 million, and is highly regarded in the Netherlands

item.title: ‘It crosses the line’ - Man Utd CEO Omar Berrada hits back at ‘negative’ social media attacks as Red Devils languish in 18th place
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-MAN CITY-MAN UTD - AFP Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada has hit back at intense supporter backlash, claiming that some recent criticism aimed at the club's hierarchy has crossed a line. The rare interview comes as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take charge of his first game against Liverpool on Sunday. Berrada addresses the mounting boardroom backlash Berrada has openly addressed the mounting frustration surrounding the club. He strongly believes that while some supporter anger is completely justified, recent relentless attacks on the club's hierarchy have gone too far. United currently sit a dismal 18th in the Premier League table after a horrendous start to the campaign . This disastrous domestic form has unsurprisingly sparked furious reactions from the passionate fanbase, both in the stands and across online platforms. Key figures in the Old Trafford boardroom have faced immense scrutiny in recent weeks. Berrada himself, alongside director of football Jason Wilcox, has been heavily targeted by angry supporters who are desperately demanding immediate sweeping changes. Crossing the line in a social media world In an interview with Sky Sports , Berrada explained how the modern digital landscape constantly amplifies negativity. He insisted that the club's leadership group is actively trying to ignore the external noise and focus on fixing the ongoing issues. "Being in this position comes naturally with the criticism and scrutiny we're going to get," Berrada admitted. "We accept it. Some of it is fair, some of it does cross the line. We do live in this world of social media, where people like to generate negative stories about the club because it drives more engagement. But we park that." Growing protests against the club ownership The venom directed at Berrada and Wilcox represents just one part of a much wider, deeply entrenched protest against the Manchester United ownership structure. Social media campaigns have aggressively called for both sporting executives to lose their jobs in recent weeks. Match-going fans have also directed their visible fury towards the boardroom during recent dire fixtures. Audible chants are now regularly heard around the stadium calling for INEOS chief and minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to walk away from his sporting project. Meanwhile, the long-standing hostility towards the Glazer family remains fiercely intense among the fanbase. Their controversial leveraged buyout in 2005 saddled the historic club with enormous financial burdens, with total debt now exceeding the £1 billion mark. Pochettino prepares for massive Liverpool test The incredibly toxic and chaotic backdrop at Old Trafford sets a daunting scene for newly appointed head coach Pochettino . The Argentine tactician faces an incredibly difficult task to galvanise a broken squad and drag the club out of the relegation zone. Pochettino will officially begin his United tenure with a massive Premier League fixture against fierce riv

item.title: Bills have been feasting on backup QBs. Here comes another
item.description: ORCHARD PARK - Unlike Joe Fagnano and Cade Klubnik before him, Miami Dolphins rookie backup quarterback Kyle McCord will have the benefit of not playing his very first career NFL snap coming off the bench cold against the AFC-leading Buffalo Bills . When the Dolphins placed starter Malik Willis on injured reserve after he was injured in their Week 9 loss to the Lions , McCord had a full practice week with starters’ reps in front of last week’s 24-22 loss to the Colts . Fagnano of the Ravens and Klubnik of the Jets did not have that luxury when they had to take over midgame for injured starters and they were both mostly helpless as they failed to lead their teams to a touchdown and combined to complete 21 of 41 passes for 228 yards with two interceptions. McCord will start Sunday when the 1-8 Dolphins visit Highmark Stadium to play the 8-1 Bills in a game that looks like a total mismatch, at least on paper. Kyle McCord gets second NFL start against Bills Last week in Indianapolis, McCord nearly led Miami to a victory as he completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards. In fact, Miami probably should have won, but now-unemployed kicker Zane Gonzalez missed two field goals and an extra point. His second field-goal miss came with 9:49 remaining and would have given the Dolphins the lead. McCord got two more possessions after that but both ended in turnovers on downs and the Colts survived. “We liked Kyle a lot coming out,” Bills coach Joe Brady said. “He's a really good football player and he's got a little more experience playing in that last game. Thought he did what he had to do. They had opportunities to win the football game, so it's going to be a huge test for us.” Huge might be a bit hyperbolic, but McCord can play the position. He began his college career as a big recruit for perennial powerhouse Ohio State and after two years as C.J. Stroud’s backup, he became the starter in 2023 and threw for 3,170 yards with 24 TDs, six interceptions, and a nation-leading 9.1 yards per attempt and 13.8 yards per completion, with 1,211 of those yards in the hands of wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. However, after an 11-0 start, McCord and the Buckeyes lost to arch-rival Michigan which cost them a chance at the Big Ten title. He entered the transfer portal before the Buckeyes’ Cotton Bowl loss to Missouri. McCord transferred to Syracuse in 2024 and played magnificently, leading the country in completions (391), attempts (592), and yards (4,779) which were all Orange school records. The Eagles picked him in the sixth round of the 2025 draft, he was released after the season and signed with the Packers, then was traded to the Dolphins at the end of training camp. “I think he'll take a good step,” Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said of McCord playing in his second game. “Just think about the first time going out there early on, the anxiety, the speed of the game, the unknown. And even in the conversations with him, how were they going to play him, and it took him a litt

item.title: An Australian captain who can play for Wales in 2027
item.description: Liam Wright had to wait four years between his fifth and six caps for Australia [Getty Images] Ospreys flanker and once-Australian captain Liam Wright will be at the Principality Stadium today to watch the Wallabies take on Wales in Cardiff. Wright knows that in less than a year, it is possible he could be playing for Australia or Wales at the World Cup in the land of his birth. The 29-year-old has made six appearances for the Wallabies, but his previous game was in July 2024. So despite being capped by the Wallabies, World Rugby regulations would allow him to play for another country three years after his previous international appearance. His eligibility to switch allegiances would start next summer, and just a few months before the World Cup begins in Australia in September 2027. Wright has Welsh heritage, with his grandfather hailing from Pembroke Dock. After more than a year out of professional rugby, Wright moved 12,000 miles to join Ospreys and wants to return to the international stage. "Test rugby is what I want to get to; it's the pinnacle and where I want to play and end up again," he said. Will an international return be for Australia or Wales? Liam Wright played in the back row for Australia against Wales in July 2024 [Getty Images] Which country Wright might play for remains to be seen. When asked about potentially representing Wales, he replied: "I imagine myself playing Test rugby and wanting to do it in a gold jersey, but I'm not going to turn down opportunities anywhere. "If the door is closed for the Wallabies and I'm playing good enough and Wales do come knocking, I'd definitely explore it. "I want to get back playing Test footy [rugby] and play for the Wallabies, but fate has a weird way of working where we've landed in Wales. "I've now got to explore the heritage. I was going past Pembroke Dock the other week and stayed there in an Airbnb and explored the area a bit, which is where my grandfather's from. "Things have a funny way of working out, so I won't rule anything out." Wright will be mindful that Wales and Australia have impressive back-row resources at their disposal. Wales head coach Steve Tandy told the Scrum V podcast in October he had not talked to Wright, who met up with the Australian camp in Cardiff this week. Australia head coach Les Kiss knows Wright well from their Queensland days. "We will always keep an eye on someone of his calibre," said Kiss. "The big thing for Liam was getting back into the game, and I've worked closely with him at the Reds for a number of years. "He was in that gym, in the physio room, throwing everything to get that shoulder right. "I loved the look in his eyes this week. He looked happy again, getting out there, plying his trade and loving the sense of living in a different environment. "I was happy to catch up with him and see how he feels good about himself again." item.title: Is it the right time to talk about winter transfers for Bayern Munich?
item.description: MUNICH, GERMANY - NOVEMBER 20: Harry Kane of FC Bayern Munich reacts after sustaining an injury during the Bundesliga 2026/27 match between FC Bayern München and 1. FC Köln at Allianz Arena on November 20, 2026 in Munich, Germany. (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich has been struck with injury after injury, taking out almost the entire attack. With hardly any attackers left, the January transfer window is an option that would allow the Bavarians to bolster a squad currently torn apart by injuries. However, Vincent Kompany wants to keep his eyes on the immediate deliverables before the winter break. After the tiring draw against 1. FC Köln—in which Harry Kane and Michael Olise also picked up injuries—Kompany was asked whether the transfer window is something Bayern are thinking about at the moment. Kompany responded in the negative, placing emphasis on utilizing the current roster. “I don’t want to talk at all about what might need to happen in two months’ time. The only thing I’m interested in right now is the games we still have ahead of us and making sure that, despite this situation, we continue to pick up points and secure wins. The players we have available now are our most important priority. Our task is to perform in these games and try, together with our fans, to keep helping each other through this situation. Everything else doesn’t matter at the moment,” said Kompany (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) BFW Commentary Kompany’s statement makes sense. The winter break is still more than a month away, and pining hopes on the transfer window is not an option right now. Luis Díaz is expected to return midweek against LOSC Lille in the Champions League. Lennart Karl and Na thaniel Brown could be his partners in attack, with Díaz potentially filling in as a temporary striker. Regardless, this is one of the biggest crises at Bayern in recent times and one that will test the resolve of the staff, management, and fans. Now, the challenge isn’t just getting the best out of very little, but also staying healthy and ending this run of injuries. Expect youth players to be called up heavily over the next month to aid the attack as the club evaluates whether to make an emergency winter signing. Join the conversation! item.title: Monza want €40m for Gustavo Varela, but is he worth it?
item.description: Monza want €40m for Gustavo Varela, but is he worth it? Serie A has several underdog stories blossoming this season on both team and player levels and is all the more worthwhile for it. One such story is of Gustavo Varela, who despite being in his debut season in Italy already looks like a man on a mission. Having scored just seven goals last season in 33 appearances while on loan at Gil Vicente from Benfica, the 21-year-old already has 11 goals in 11 outings this term. These are numbers few were expecting, that too for a team not expected to have a great campaign. Monza are again looking down the barrel, and between their early-season slump and several of their counterparts looking keen to at least put up a fight, things are not looking good for the Brianzoli. But Varela is unquestionably a shining light. Even if he doesn’t manage to help keep Monza up, he is turning enough heads to be able to earn himself a move and not have to try his luck in Serie B. Some even believe a mid-season switch to not be out of question. It would make sense if Monza were to capitalise on his hype knowing they might go down anyway, and there’s previous for this. But is it too soon for Varela? Is he really already worth €40 million. Despite market valuations, the price of a player comes down to however much the buying party is willing to conjure up. And while there are several success stories featuring players who move early and thrive, there are several others — often more frequent — of players who move too early and for too lofty a price tag which they never manage to justify. In recent years alone there are several cautionary tales. Krzysztof Piątek, case in point, looked like the next great striker of his generation before moving to Milan after just half a season with Genoa, and while his numbers mostly remain respectable, the now Al-Duhail man never reached the heights that were expected of him during his short stint at the Marassi. Similarly, Juan Manuel Iturbe, a darling of the video game folk, arrived at Roma amid much fanfare before his career plateaued. After struggling in Europe, he has gone on to have a respectable career in the Americas and is currently at his boyhood club, Cerro Porteño. In fact, one could even argue that Juventus that did not quite get what they were hoping for when they splurged €70 million on Dušan Vlahović to pry him away from Fiorentina in January 2022. All that said, the fact of the matter remains that the current market is a fidgeting, impatient one. Clubs spend money not just to get a player early but to deprive rivals of the chance as well, not only looking at what profits they can make but also on how much loss they can digest. Moreover, the current financial resplendence of English football makes a €40m price tag chump change for all Premier League clubs and manageable for even several Championship ones. That spectre further triggers mania among European clubs, who find their windows of opportunity ever shrinking. Varela’s tac

item.description: Serie A: Lazio vs. Lecce – Probable line-ups and where to watch on TV Lazio and Lecce kick off the return of Serie A action at 14.00 GMT following the recent international break, and Gennaro Gattuso is expected to have Davide Frattesi available despite his withdrawal from the Italy national team squad last week. Hosts Lazio sit at the top of the Serie A standings after 11 matches of the 2026-27 season with nine victories and two draws totalling 29 points thus far. They are one of two teams still unbeaten in the Italian top flight after 11 games, along with city rivals Roma. item.title: 'To protect integrity of Australian Cricket': CA drops big statement on Cummins captaincy amid sandpapergate row
item.description: Cricket Australia (CA) has thrown its support behind Pat Cummins, confirming that he will remain Australia's Test captain for the New Zealand series next month despite allegations from former teammates about his involvement in the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal. The CA board met on Friday (local time) to discuss Cummins' position as captain and decided to back the 33-year-old unanimously. CA chair David Boon and CEO Todd Greenberg also met Cummins in Sydney to discuss his welfare, the support needed by the team and the upcoming series against New Zealand. “The CA Board met to ensure measures are in place to protect the integrity of Australian cricket and the welfare of all concerned. As part of this meeting, the Board resolved to express its unanimous support for Pat Cummins as captain given ongoing speculation about his position,” a CA statement read. “CA chair David Boon and CEO Todd Greenberg met with Cummins in Sydney on Friday and discussed several issues including his welfare, support required for the team and the forthcoming series against New Zealand.” Boon said the board wanted to guide Australian cricket through the controversy while allowing players and support staff to share any information they had about the 2018 tour of South Africa. Boon said the forum announced earlier this week would provide an opportunity for those involved in the tour to discuss their accounts. CA has said it will publish the forum's Terms of Reference in due course. “That’s what the independent forum we announced this week is about and the board encourages all players and support staff to tell and discuss their stories there. We will be publishing the Terms of Reference in due course,” Boon said. “We’ve expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa. “We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat’s integrity has been compromised.” Cummins also issued a statement thanking Boon and Greenberg for their support. He said being Australia's captain was a responsibility he had always taken seriously and welcomed the board's decision to speak to him and other players and staff involved in the 2018 tour. “It meant a lot to speak with David and Todd today. Being Australian captain carries with it an awesome responsibility. I never have and never will take that lightly,” Cummins said. “David and Todd have a very tough job navigating cricket through all of this and I commend them for reaching out to me and to many of the players and staff from 2018.” Cummins also said he fully supported the independent forum and would attend to hear what players and staff had to say about the events of the South Africa tour. “There will be a lot of difficult conversations but that is what’s needed,” Cummins said. “Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team i

item.title: Scott McTominay: Man United offered chance to bring Napoli star back to Old Trafford
item.description: Scott McTominay: Man United offered chance to bring Napoli star back to Old Trafford Manchester United made the surprise decision to allow Scott McTominay to join Napoli in 2024, under former manager Erik ten Hag. The Red Devils replaced the Scot with Manuel Ugarte and it would turn out to be a disastrous decision. Brought in to replace Casemiro at Old Trafford, the Uruguayan was a disappointment, and soon became a peripheral figure at the Theatre of Dreams. Ugarte is currently sidelined after rupturing his ACL at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The Brazilian eventually left this summer with his head held high, and the English giants ended up spending over £150 million on Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba to fill his boots. Unfortunately, the trio are yet to live up to the task, with United struggling to control the midfield in games and now sitting 18th in the Premier League table after 10 games. The situation has prompted talk of further reinforcements in the middle of the park in 2027, with rumours of a possible homecoming for McTominay refusing to go away. McTominay’s spectacular rise in Italy McTominay hit the ground running in Serie A, helping Napoli win the league in his debut campaign and finishing as the Serie A MVP. The 29-year-old was equally decisive last season, with his team finishing second behind Inter Milan. The Scottish midfielder’s spectacular rise in Italy has generated a very poor impression of United’s decision-making. Meanwhile, former manager Ten Hag has recently revealed that he was vehemently opposed to McTominay’s departure . The Scot’s contract expires in 2028 and he has yet to sign a new deal, adding to speculation regarding his future. It now, however, appears that the Red Devils could have the opportunity to rectify their error and bring their prodigal son home. United alert to McTominay’s Napoli situation According to TEAMtalk , United could have the opportunity to bring their former academy graduate back in 2027. The report states: “Scott McTominay is heading into 2027 with one eye on a possible return to the Premier League, with former club Manchester United being made aware of an opportunity to bring him back to Old Trafford, TEAMtalk understands.” The report confirms that Napoli are keen to keep hold of McTominay, but adds that “the two parties remain some way apart in their negotiations, with no breakthrough currently in sight.” Intermediaries are already working on the player’s next move, with the report adding: “TEAMtalk can reveal that intermediaries are now working on potential options for McTominay heading into 2027, with a return to English football firmly among the possibilities being explored.” “Manchester United have been informed of his potential availability, and TEAMtalk understands the idea of bringing their former academy graduate back to Old Trafford has not been dismissed out of hand.” AC Milan, Juventus, Chelsea and clubs from Saudi Arabia are also hot on his heels, and the report stat

item.title: Why Nigeria is seeking stronger EU partnership to combat terrorism – Defence Minister
item.description: Reveals Troops Intercepted Over 400 Starlinks Devices Linked to Terrorist Networks. By: Kingsley Omonobi The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (rtd), has reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to a comprehensive, whole-of-government strategy to combat terrorism, while seeking stronger security cooperation with the European Union (EU). Musa made this known at the third edition of the Schuman Security and Defence Forum held at the European Parliament in Brussels, Belgium, where he represented Nigeria. Disclosing that the Armed Forces of Nigeria were deploying intelligence-led operations, advanced surveillance systems, unmanned aerial platforms and military artificial intelligence to weaken terrorist networks, the Minister told the gathering that troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted more than 400 Starlink communication devices linked to terrorist networks in the North-East in May 2026. A statement issued by the Special Adviser on Media to the Minister, Leah Katung-Babatunde quoted the minister saying Nigeria was shifting from a predominantly military approach to a coordinated counterterrorism strategy involving intelligence gathering, law enforcement, community engagement and socio-economic interventions. He explained that terrorism remained a complex security challenge fuelled by economic vulnerabilities, porous borders, local grievances and transnational organised crime. The minister said the strategy, guided by Nigeria’s National Counter Terrorism Strategy (NACTEST), reflected the administration’s determination to address both the immediate threats posed by terrorist groups and the underlying factors sustaining insecurity. Addressing the growing use of emerging technologies by violent extremist groups, Musa highlighted Nigeria’s efforts to counter the illicit deployment of drones, digital communication devices and satellite technologies. He said the Armed Forces of Nigeria were deploying intelligence-led operations, advanced surveillance systems, unmanned aerial platforms and military artificial intelligence to weaken terrorist networks. He particularly disclosed that troops of Operation Hadin Kai intercepted more than 400 Starlink communication devices linked to terrorist networks in the North-East in May 2026. Musa also highlighted the Ministry of Defence’s efforts to promote indigenous defence innovation through research and partnerships with the private sector. He called for stronger collaboration with the European Union in counter-drone technologies, digital forensics and satellite intelligence to enhance Nigeria’s capacity to respond to evolving security threats. On the financial networks sustaining terrorism, the minister stressed the need to dismantle criminal economies, including kidnapping for ransom, illegal mining, cattle rustling and illicit arms trafficking. item.title: Crystal Palace eye January reunion between Thomas Frank and Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney
item.description: Al Ahli vs Al Nassr : Saudi Pro League - Getty Images Sport Crystal Palace are considering a January swoop for Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney as new boss Thomas Frank looks to reunite with his former forward. The 30-year-old England international is open to a Premier League comeback as the relegation-threatened Eagles search for firepower. Euro ambitions drive return hopes According to talkSPORT , Palace have identified Toney as a winter option after promising Frank the resources needed to strengthen a squad rooted to the foot of the table . Having previously worked under the Danish coach at Brentford, the forward is keen to boost his chances of making England's Euro 2028 squad. Those international hopes recently took a knock when he failed to move a court date clashing with the tournament . Prolific spell highlights goalscoring pedigree Toney left Brentford for Saudi Arabia in a £40 million transfer during the summer of 2024 , departing west London with a proven top-flight record of 36 goals in 85 Premier League appearances. Since arriving at Al-Ahli, his output in front of goal has become even more formidable across both domestic and continental competition. The 30-year-old has amassed 87 goals in just 109 outings in all competitions for the Saudi Pro League side, playing a central role in helping them lift back-to-back AFC Champions League Elite titles. His blistering form has continued into the current campaign, where he has already registered 15 goals in 16 appearances, including 14 strikes in 10 league matches to top the division's scoring charts. Selhurst Park attack desperately struggles That clinical edge stands in stark contrast to Palace's glaring issues in the final third this season. Across their opening 10 Premier League fixtures, the south London club have collected just seven points and scored only 10 goals, failing to find the net in half of those matches and managing a single strike across their last four outings. No member of the current squad has scored more than four goals in all competitions, a drought worsened by last season's top scorer Ismaila Sarr being ruled out until December through injury. Jean-Philippe Mateta, who struck 19 times last term, has also endured a difficult campaign with just one goal across all competitions so far. Coventry trip launches survival bid Before any winter recruitment can take place, Frank begins his tenure on Saturday when Palace travel to the CBS Arena to face Coventry City . Victory over the Sky Blues would lift the Eagles out of the relegation zone and leapfrog their opponents in the standings. Until Sarr returns and January arrives, finding an immediate spark up front remains Frank's most urgent challenge.

item.title: Harden passes Bryant for 50-point games
item.description: Harden joined the Cavaliers in February after three years with the Los Angeles Clippers [Getty Images] James Harden scored 51 points to move third on the all-time list for 50-point NBA games as the Cleveland Cavaliers beat the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in the NBA Cup. The 37-year-old made all 14 of his free throws as his recorded his 26th 50-point game to move above the legendary Kobe Bryant. Harden, who also made six rebounds and provided six assists at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, had not passed 50 points since scoring 55 for the Los Angeles Clippers in November 2025. Legendary centre Wilt Chamberlain holds the NBA record ⁠with 118 50-point games, while Michael Jordan is second with 31. "When you talk about just basketball, obviously Wilt was elite, but you got Mike and Kobe - shooting guard position, the best to ever do it - so just to be in that conversation, it's very humbling and it's definitely special," said an emotional Harden. Aged 37 years and 86 days, he is the fourth oldest player to score 50 points in a game. "What excites me a lot is even being in my 18th year learning how to still be impactful," said Harden, the ninth highest scorer in NBA history with 29,633 points. "It's easy when you're young - 23, 24, you run around, you jump high and can move fast and get by. Now it's like, you're not as fast. "That's the evolution of James Harden and figuring that out. "Tonight was a confidence-booster that I can do it at a high level still." The Cavaliers travel to the Chicago Bulls in the NBA on Tuesday.

item.title: Tri-West punches ticket to state title game with thrilling win over Indian Creek
item.description: TRAFALGAR - Twelve years since their last state title appearance, the Tri-West Bruins (12-2) broke their dry spell with a 24-21 win over the previously-unbeaten Indian Creek Braves (12-1) in Class 3A semistate action on Friday. The Bruins redeemed a Week 5 loss to the Braves and cried tears of joy after their victory - one win away from being crowned 3A champions. “We worked so hard since we were little kids and we spoke it into existence that if we didn’t win or at least didn’t go to state this year, it was a failure,” said Tri-West senior Carter Cummings. “We really took that to heart and I think it shows man.” Tri-West needed under two minutes to draw first blood. After a good return put them at their own 45, senior quarterback Jack Sorgi took the snap 11 yards for a touchdown. That closed out a seven-play drive with 8:11 left in the opening frame. “That first drive was very important because all week we stressed how good their defense was,” said Tri-West coach Jason Ward. “This is a top defense and just showed Indian Creek that we can move the ball on them. Just kind of make them second guess themselves (like),’ Can we stop them tonight?’ It’s hell of a team. One good defense, and yes, that first drive was very important.” The Braves fumbled on a punt return, which gave the ball back to the Bruins. Eleven plays later, sophomore Jax Clayton put Tri-West up 10-0 with a field goal from 27 yards out. With 5:30 left in quarter two, Indian Creek’s offense was in scoring position, but defensive back Seth Mohr nabbed an interception in the endzone and gave the ball back to the Bruins. “We knew they were going to take shots, and it was all about limiting the big plays and I think we did a great job at that tonight," Mohr said. Indian Creek’s defense held up in the final few minutes of the second frame. After securing their second turnover of the game, the Bruins came up empty on their next offensive possession. Indian Creek senior Rhys Shand came down with a 35-yard touchdown that put the Braves on the board, 10-7. Tri-West got the final offensive possession of the first half and reached its own 15 but Indian Creek’s defense kept their deficit to within a field goal heading into halftime. After Tri-West missed its own attempt, Indian Creek evened the score with a field goal with nine minutes left in the third quarter. After an interception was called off due to a pass interference call on Indian Creek, the ball was placed at the 13 before senior Braxton Fleece drove in a 4-yard touchdown with 1:16 left in quarter three. The Braves countered with a field goal, but the Bruins needed just three offensive plays to get a touchdown on the board. Sorgi connected with an open Cummings on a 36-yard score that gave Tri-West a 24-13 lead with 7:30 left in the fourth quarter. Indian Creek, the semistate host, didn’t go down without a fight. Defensive lineman Riley Emberton scooped up a fumble and took it back about 25 yards for a score. The Braves scored on their

item.title: Sultan arrives Benin to honour Oba Ewuare II on 10th coronation anniversary
item.description: The Sultan of Sokoto, His Eminence Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, has arrived Benin City, Edo State, ahead of the 10th coronation anniversary of the Oba of Benin, Omo N’Oba N’Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo, Oba Ewuare II, Oba of Benin. The aircraft conveying the Sultan touched ground at the Oba Akenzua II Airport in the Edo State capital 25 minutes after departing the Samuel Ladoke Akintola International Airport, Ibadan, Oyo State, at 5:05 p.m. on Friday, November 20. In a statement by Prince Bashir Adefaka on behalf of the Media Team of the Sultan of Sokoto, noted that the Sultan was received by senior members of the Oba of Benin-in-Council at the airport. He was accompanied on the flight by the Galadiman Gerin Sokoto, His Royal Highness Alhaji Aliyu Attahiru Galadanci, and former Director-General, National Broadcasting Commission, NBC, Mallam Danladi Bako, Kogunan Sokoto. The Sultan arrived Ibadan on a weeklong South-West working visit on Sunday, November 15, starting off his activities with participation in the 11th General Assembly of the Muslim Ummah of South West Nigeria, MUSWEN, as special guest of honour. The Sultan also performed his duty as Chancellor of the University of Ibadan on Tuesday, November 17, supported by his Pro-Chancellor and Chairman Governing Council, Chief Bisi Akande, as well as the new Vice-Chancellor, Professor Peter Olamakinde Olapegba, among others. On Wednesday, he travelled from his Ibadan to Saki to partake – as Chairman of the Day – in the official commissioning of the 500-seat Alhaji Azeez Adedokun Olowolagba Information and Communication Technology, ICT, Centre built and donated to the College of Nursing Sciences, Muslim Medical Foundation Saki, by Alhaji Mudasiru Adedokun Olowolagba, in memory of his late father. On Thursday, the Sultan paid a courtesy call on the Aseyin of Iseyin, Oba Sefiu Olawale Adeyemi III (Ajirotutu I), who will be celebrating his third coronation anniversary on December 11. He also witnessed the award ceremony by the Iseyin Kingdom in honour of legal luminary and philanthropist, Barrister Ahmed Raji (SAN). On Friday, the Sultan of Sokoto paid a courtesy visit to the palace of the Olubadan of Ibadan Land, where Oba Rashidi Ladoja, Arusa I, assisted by Olubadan-in-Council, received him. Both monarchs then proceeded to the Bodija Muslim Community Central Mosque, Ibadan, where they observed their Jumat service led by the Chief Imam, Sheikh Hakeem Ibrahim. He the left for Benin City, where he was first received by members of the Oba of Benin-in-Council and then later by the royal host himself in his palace the same Friday night. item.title: ‘They’re In Trouble’ — Hall of Fame HC Bill Parcells Has Some Bad News for Aaron Rodgers’ Steelers
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers. The Pittsburgh Steelers briefly had control of the AFC North in early November, but their latest loss has changed the conversation around Mike McCarthy’s team. A defeat against the Cincinnati Bengals exposed problems on both sides of the ball and handed a division rival sole possession of first place. Now, Hall of Fame coach Bill Parcells has weighed in on Pittsburgh’s position, and his assessment offers little comfort for Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers. Bill Parcells Warns Aaron Rodgers’ Steelers After Heavy Bengals Loss During an appearance on “Football Doesn’t Lie,” Parcells was asked to rate several NFL teams on a scale of 1 to 10 based on how worried they should be. His response about Pittsburgh was direct, especially after the Steelers suffered a 38-18 loss to Cincinnati in Week 10. “I think they’re in trouble. Their division rival, Cincinnati, just beat them handily. That’s not a good sign,” Parcells said. He also pointed to the AFC North race, adding, “That division is pretty well balanced, but Cincinnati definitely looks like it has a strong hold on that.” The result carried major consequences for Pittsburgh. The Steelers entered the matchup at 6-2, but the defeat dropped them to 6-3 and second place in the division. Cincinnati improved to 7-2 and extended its winning streak to five games. Rodgers has thrown for 2,014 yards, 15 touchdowns, and six interceptions this season, with an 86.4 passer rating. item.title: Harry Kane out for a ‘few months’ as Bayern Munich confirm ankle ligament tear
item.description: Harry Kane faces the "next few months" on the sidelines after suffering a torn left ankle ligament during Bayern Munich ’s 1-1 draw against Cologne on Friday. The injury occurred when Cologne defender Joel Schmied intercepted Michael Olise’s low cross at the back post, clattering into the Ballon d’Or winner’s left leg on the follow-through. Though the England captain got back to his feet after treatment, he was unable to continue and hobbled off the pitch accompanied by two physios. Following an assessment by the club’s medical team, Bayern confirmed Kane had sustained a torn syndesmotic ligament and "will therefore be sidelined for the next few months". It is a major setback for Kane, who won the Ballon d’Or last month and then became the most-capped England men’s player of all time last week, surpassing the previous record held by Peter Shilton. Kane received treatment but was unable to continue on Friday night (Getty) Kane scored 73 goals last season to earn the Ballon d’Or and had made a flying start to the current campaign, registering 10 goals and 10 assists in 16 games for Bayern across all competitions. He also scored eight goals in six Nations League games to help England top their group as he took his overall international tally to 93 goals in 127 caps. England learned on Friday that they will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, which will be a rematch of the two teams meeting at the same stage of the World Cup back in July. Thomas Tuchel’s side won that game 2-1 thanks to a brace from Jude Bellingham, and the two-legged quarter-final will be played in late March. Kane will hope that he is back in time for that tie, but Bayern’s statement indicates that he will not be seen on the pitch for the remainder of 2026 or the early weeks of 2027. Kane’s injury is a real blow for Bayern (Tom Weller/PA) Bayern also suffered another injury blow on Friday night as Michael Olise failed to return for the second half. The club issued an update on Olise’s condition after the game. The statement read: “Michael Olise has been diagnosed with a contusion of the foot. The French attacking player will receive treatment over the coming days.”

item.title: B1G volleyball tournament brings Illinois freshman back to hometown roots
item.description: FISHERS — The entirety of Friday has been a surreal experience for Hamilton Southeastern High School grad Madi Miles. Now an outside hitter for the Illinois volleyball team, the 6-1 freshman is back in her hometown for the inaugural Big Ten volleyball tournament, which began this weekend at the Fishers Event Center. The Illini made the two-hour bus ride from Champaign on Friday morning, allowing Miles to take in all the familiar sights as they headed to the venue. That in itself was a "weird" and "crazy" experience, Miles said. And then they arrived at the facility. The 2025 Indiana Miss Volleyball finalist estimates she ran into at least five people she knew while walking around the events center, the encounters ranging from former teachers and the dad of former high school teammate Jasmine Daniels, to Fishers mayor Scott Fadness and former HSE athletic director Jim Self, who grabbed a photo with Miles before the team departed for practice. "It's been really cool seeing all the familiar faces — and that's just today," Miles said. "We don't even play (tonight), so I can't wait to see what Saturday's going to be like." As the regular season began winding down, Miles' high school coach, Jason Young, was pushing for Hamilton Southeastern to host Illini practices for the duration of their stay. "My mom was in contact with him and keeping me updated," she laughed. "It's so weird being back," Miles later added. The entire team strolled the athletic corridor, checking out pictures of their teammate from her days as a two-time Class 4A state champion with the powerhouse Royals. Inside the gym, the video boards displayed a graphic welcoming Miles home with her two most recent team photos and the message "Once a Royal, always a Royal." And, yes, the team made sure to get a photo with the signage before starting practice. "My teammates are amazing," Miles said. "They've been really helping me and pushing me." Those teammates, she continued, have helped fuel her recent run of success, maintaining trust in her and feeding her balls in spots where they know she can be successful. To wit, Miles racked up 106 kills over an eight-match stretch between October and November, then collected six kills, two digs and two blocks in the regular-season finale at Iowa. For the season, Miles has 129 kills (.204 hit%), 29 digs and 10 blocks in 44 sets played for the seventh-seeded Illini, who open against Washington at 6 p.m. Saturday. "Everyone on this team trusts each other and everyone likes to push each other and make each other better," she said. "That really helps." Things should settle down — at least a little — for Miles on Friday night with a couple hours of free time built in after film, during which she'll (finally) be able to catch up with her family, including twin sister, Raegan, an outside hitter at Taylor.
