item.title: 'It's not a revenge mission' - Zinedine Zidane downplays World Cup heartbreak as France draw Spain in Nations League blockbuster
item.description: Italy v France - UEFA Nations League 2026/27 Group A1 MD5 - Getty Images Sport France head coach Zinedine Zidane has insisted that his side’s upcoming Nations League quarter-final against Spain is not fueled by a desire for retribution. The legendary figure is preparing his squad for a heavyweight double-header against the reigning world champions following the tournament draw on Friday. A heavyweight clash in the quarter-finals The knockout stage draw for the UEFA Nations League has delivered a blockbuster tie, with Zidane’s France set to face reigning European and world champions Spain. After securing top spot in their group, Les Bleus were hoping for a favorable path, but instead find themselves pitted against their greatest recent nemesis. The two-legged tie will represent the most significant tactical test for Zidane since he took the reins of the national team. Scheduling for the tie has also been confirmed, with the first leg taking place in Valencia on 25 March, followed by a decisive return leg at the Stade de France three days later. History suggests a difficult task ahead for the French, who have struggled against their neighbors across the border. Spain have emerged victorious in each of the last three competitive meetings between the two nations, including a pivotal 2-1 victory in the Euro 2024 semi-finals and a high-scoring 5-4 thriller in the previous Nations League cycle. Most notably, the memories of a comprehensive 2-0 defeat in last summer’s World Cup semi-final still loom large over the French squad. Zidane shuts down World Cup revenge talk Zidane has poured cold water on talk of a revenge mission, swiftly waving away the narrative that his side is out to settle old scores. Despite the undeniably high stakes and the bitter memories of their recent World Cup semi-final heartbreak, the legendary midfielder-turned-manager insists his squad is looking strictly to the future rather than dwelling on past disappointments. "We knew we were going to draw a strong team. It will therefore be Spain, the reigning world champion. We know them perfectly, but the observation has been made on their last matches and we will analyze all that with my staff. To go far in a competition, you have to, in any case, play and eliminate the best teams," Zidane said, as quoted by Foot Mercato . "It is not a revenge for the semi-final of the World Cup, but another competition with a new group. And the objective remains the same: go to the Final Four and win the Nations League." Building towards the March window Zidane maintains that the continuous tactical and personnel evolution of his squad, when combined with the distinct environment of an entirely new tournament, essentially renders any historical results or past encounters completely irrelevant to their current campaign. item.title: How Marc Marquez can be crowned MotoGP champion in Portuguese GP sprint
item.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez had his first mathematical opportunity to clinch his 10th world championship title – and eighth in the premier class – at the Qatar Grand Prix, but he was unable to seal it. However, the Ducati rider has another chance over the Portuguese Grand Prix weekend, which he himself has described as his “first real championship match point”. With 74 points still available (37 in Portimao and 37 in Valencia), the Spaniard holds a 60-point advantage over Jorge Martin and a 74-point lead over Marco Bezzecchi, meaning he could mathematically clinch the world championship on Saturday after the sprint race. The scenarios for Marc Marquez to clinch the 2026 title at the Portuguese GP are straightforward, as they depend solely on his own results. In general, Marquez cannot lose more than 23 points to Martin over the weekend, meaning he would clinch the title if he outscored the Spaniard by two points across the weekend. Marquez needs to score just one point over the entire weekend to mathematically eliminate Bezzecchi from the title race. Therefore, even if Marquez fails to clinch the title on Saturday, he will still have a strong chance of doing so on Sunday. How Marquez can seal the title in Portuguese GP sprint He will be champion if he wins the sprint race. He will be champion if he finishes second in the sprint and Martin is third or lower. He will be champion if he finishes third in the sprint and Martin is fifth or lower. He will be champion if he finishes fourth in the sprint and Martin is sixth or lower. He will be champion if he finishes fifth in the sprint and Martin is seventh or lower. He will be champion if he finishes sixth in the sprint and Martin is eighth or lower. He will be champion if he finishes seventh in the sprint and Martin is ninth or lower. He will be champion if he finishes eighth in the sprint and Martin is 10th or lower. Why would a 37-point lead over Martin be enough? A 37-point advantage would be sufficient because, in the event of a tie in the final championship standings, Marquez would be crowned champion ahead of Martin on countback, having won more races this season. The Ducati rider currently has eight victories compared with Martin’s one, meaning the Spaniard could finish the season with an eight-to-three advantage in wins if Martin triumphs at both Portimao and Valencia. What does Jorge Martin need to keep the title fight alive until Valencia? Martin currently trails Marquez by 60 points and would lose the title on countback in the event of a tie. The Aprilia rider therefore needs to leave Portimao no more than 36 points behind the championship leader. Martin needs to gain at least 24 points on Marquez and hope the Ducati rider scores no more than 13 points over the entire weekend. How can Marco Bezzecchi stay in the title fight? item.title: Lakeland stuns Chaminade-Madonna; LCS advances, Lake Wales falls in OT
item.description: HOLLYWOOD — For 1 1/2 quarters, it appeared that traveling to South Florida to face a national powerhouse on the road was going to be too much for Lakeland to overcome, especially coming off the emotional of last week’s victory. The listless Dreadnaughts came up an 82-yard touchdown pass on the first play of the game and trailed by three touchdowns. However, Lakeland gradually morphed into the No. 10 team in the nation that it is, scored four touchdowns before allowing another point and held on to a 28-27 victory over Hollywood Chaminade-Madonna on Friday night. Lakeland (11-1) has guaranteed itself a spot in the state semifinals. The Dreadnaughts are the only 2-0 team in Pool A. St. Thomas’ Aquinas, after defeating Venice, 38-16 on Friday, and Chaminade-Madonna (9-3) are both 1-1. The winner of St. Thomas-Chaminade next week will be 2-1 and advance with Lakeland, regardless if Lakeland wins or loses to Venice after Thanksgiving. “We ain’t done yet,” defensive back Ahmaad Watts said. “We’re coming to take it all. We were counted down, but we’re coming to take it all. Be ready.” Here’s how Lakeland pulled off its dramatic come-from-behind victory. It starts with Hendrix Lakeland quarterback Kelin Hendrix had an even bigger week after finishing with 182 yards to total offense last week. With Lakeland committed to grinding it out on the ground, Hendrix rushed for 202 yards on 15 carries and completed just one pass for about 24 yards. He scored three consecutive touchdowns to send Lakeland to a 22-21 lead with the go-ahead scoring coming on a 23-yard run late in the third quarter. “He’s the best player in the state,” Lakeland coach Marvin Frazier said. “I tell the college coaches they see him at quarterback, they don't know where to play him. But hey guys, when you put a kid on the field, you drop him off against St. Thomas, he's the best one. You drop him off against Chaminade, he's the best one. What else do you want to say? He's the best player.” Hendrix began the comeback by rushing three times for 58 yards on an 80-yard scoring drive capped with his 26-yard touchdown run at 8:40 of the second quarter. His 1-yard touchdown run on fourth-and-1 made it a one-score game, 21-15, with 4:28 to play in the third quarter. “Offensively, we came out a little flat, but we know that it was just little things that we had,” Hendrix said. “We were one tackle away every time we ran the ball, one tackle away from breaking out. All we had to do is finish throughout the plays, believe in what we got going on, believe in the play calling, and just work as a team, stay focused and stayed together.” Ground game vs. air attack Lakeland rushed for 401 yards to overcome Chaminade-Madonna’s passing attack. In addition to Hendrix’ day, Ahnarri Cooper ran for 119 yards on 12 carries, including a 79-yard run for Lakeland’s last score. Xavion Mitchell ran for 79 yards on 18 carries. item.title: Countries race to secure COP31 deal after fossil fuel row
item.description: The COP31 climate talks spilled into Saturday as countries raced to secure a deal after a draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels, exposing deep divisions over how to tackle global warming. Nearly 200 nations remained deadlocked after two weeks of grinding UN talks in Turkey, with negotiators working through the night after missing their scheduled Friday finish amid feuds over energy, science and finance. Australia, which is presiding over the COP31 negotiations, raced against the clock to produce a third draft deal, with many delegates due to catch flights home. “We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet,” COP31 President Murat Kurum, who is Turkey’s environment minister, told an assembly late Friday that approved some technical matters. Midway through his opening address, Kurum was forced to pause while a protester shouted “You are killing the future!” before being escorted from the hall. Expectations of a major breakthrough have been low at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. The summit follows a string of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia and unfolds as a super El Nino pattern amplifies the risk of further extreme weather. A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels, a flashpoint at UN climate talks where producers such as Saudi Arabia have fiercely resisted such calls. A second, pared-down draft released on Thursday stripped away all mentions of fossil fuels — sending negotiators rushing back to the bargaining table. The European Union said the revised draft “risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit”. A dozen European and developing countries — from France to Panama and the Solomon Islands — released a letter Friday insisting that the deal include “a clear transition away from fossil fuels”. Panama, which also signed the letter, threatened to walk away from the talks. The country’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, is a vocal critic of the climate negotiations, accusing a “petroleum mafia” of blocking progress. Meanwhile, the OPEC oil cartel wrote on X that its head, Haitham Al Ghais, met Russian presidential climate envoy Ruslan Edelgeriev at COP31 to discuss “the importance of inclusive and balanced approaches across all multilateral environmental fora”. – ‘Clean electrification’ – Australia’s Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who shuttled between delegations to seek compromises, said Friday he would work “for as long as it takes, to get the job done”. The draft “cover decision” proposes a target to electrify the global economy — a push to replace technologies that burn fossil fuels directly, like diesel cars and gas heating, with electric alternatives. The goal is championed by COP31 hosts Turkey and Australia, who tout “electrification” as integral to tackling concerns over energy security and sluggish global progress in cutting heat-trapping emissions. “Electri

item.title: Chelsea threaten Barcelona’s plans to sign long-term centre-back target – report
item.description: Chelsea threaten Barcelona’s plans to sign long-term centre-back target – report Barcelona’s pursuit of Alessandro Bastoni has become more complicated after Chelsea have emerged as serious contenders for the Inter Milan defender, creating additional competition for one of Hansi Flick’s preferred defensive targets. According to recent reports from TEAMtalk , Chelsea have entered the picture as they assess options to strengthen their defence, while Barcelona continue to remain interested in the 27-year-old Italian international. Bastoni’s situation in Italy could become increasingly important over the coming months. Notably, his current agreement with Inter expires in 2028, and the Italian club would prefer to secure an extension rather than risk entering the final year of his contract without an agreement. However, with several European heavyweights monitoring his situation, Inter face an important decision over his future next summer. Chelsea’s interest complicates Barcelona’s pursuit Chelsea have entered the race for Alessandro Bastoni. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) Chelsea’s involvement is a significant development for Barcelona, particularly because the Premier League club can offer considerable financial resources. Now under former manager Xabi Alonso, the London side is looking for a left-footed centre-back, just like Barcelona. In fact, Bastoni’s representatives have already assessed Chelsea as a potential destination, with discussions taking place as part of their evaluation of the market. The report also suggests that Barcelona’s interest has become a bit doubtful because of uncertainty over whether Flick fully supports the proposed signing . That uncertainty could prove important, as Bastoni wants assurances about his role before committing to a move, meaning Barcelona would need to explain to him that he has a central place in their sporting project. Inter want to secure Bastoni’s future Inter Milan want to renew Bastoni’s contract. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Amid all this, Inter are aware that Bastoni’s contractual position could attract further attention if negotiations over an extension remain unresolved. His existing deal expires at the end of the 2027/28 season, meaning he would be able to negotiate a pre-contract agreement with foreign clubs from January 2028 if he did not renew. However, Inter are not necessarily preparing to sell, knowing that Bastoni himself has previously been described as comfortable in Milan. The possibility of a departure is therefore dependent on the outcome of future negotiations over a new contract and not the number of interested clubs.

item.title: Las Vegas starting grid shaken up after penalties for Antonelli and others
item.description: With five drivers receiving grid penalties for the upcoming Las Vegas Grand Prix , this is what the provisional starting grid looks like for tomorrow's race. With almost a quarter of the drivers having grid penalties due to exceeding the maximum amount of power unit components allowed over the course of the season, the starting grid will look quite different in Las Vegas. Max Verstappen inherits pole from Kimi Antonelli, who has a five-place penalty for taking a new internal combustion engine this weekend. George Russell will join his old rival on the front row of the grid, while Antonelli will have to start from sixth place. The second row will feature Lando Norris and Isack Hadjar, while Arvid Lindblad completes the top five. Racing Bulls talent Arvid Lindblad will start in fifth place - Photo: Race Pictures Racing Bulls talent Arvid Lindblad will start in fifth place - Photo: Race Pictures Oscar Piastri originally qualified in seventh place, but because of a 10-place penalty, he will drop to P17 on the grid. This means that both Ferrari drivers can move up a position after Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were already eliminated in Q2, qualifying in P11 and P12 respectively. After the session, the Monegasque driver was not satisfied at all : "Of course, there's a mistake in Q2 that we pay the price of, but I think that is following a lot of frustration building up with a lot of mistakes with the way we managed everything, traffic, and other things. And that doesn't help particularly on a track like this where it's all about tyres. You've got to put tyres in the right window." Three more drivers with penalties will start further down the grid. Carlos Sainz and Lance Stroll both have 10-place penalties, while Oliver Bearman will start from P22 after participating only in Q1 in an attempt to give his teammate Rafael Camara a tow. item.title: United States expected to host 2028 Copa America in second consecutive edition on American soil
item.description: Argentina v Colombia - CONMEBOL Copa America USA 2024: Final - Getty Images Sport Organisers are formalising plans for the United States to stage the 2028 Copa America, with an official announcement anticipated soon. The tournament will mark the second straight edition of South America's premier international competition held on American soil. Confederations finalise joint hosting talks According to The Athletic , all parties now expect the 2028 competition to return to the US following extensive discussions between CONMEBOL and CONCACAF that began in December 2025. Anonymous sources confirmed the host nation is not yet finalised, while Brazilian publication Globo also reported on Friday night that an announcement is imminent. Once confirmed, the US will have hosted three of the last five editions between 2016 and 2028. Commercial success outweighs previous controversies When the two confederations jointly organised the 2024 tournament, all 10 South American nations were joined by six CONCACAF guests: the US, Mexico, Canada, Panama, Costa Rica and Jamaica. Over 1.5 million supporters attended the 16-team event, which generated the majority of CONMEBOL's $319 million in national team competition revenue that year. However, the 2024 edition also drew scrutiny. Players and coaches criticised stadium playing surfaces, while Argentina's 1-0 final win over Colombia at Miami's Hard Rock Stadium was delayed by roughly 80 minutes due to dangerous crowd issues. The hosts also exited at the group stage, leading Gregg Berhalter to be replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, who coached the team at the World Cup before joining Manchester United . Packed calendar shapes summer scheduling The report states that CONCACAF nations will again have a pathway to qualify in 2028, though the exact number of spots and qualification process remain unspecified. Scheduling will require careful coordination because Los Angeles hosts the Summer Olympics starting on July 14, 2028, the exact calendar date of the 2024 final, with the US football team set to compete under coach Steve Cherundolo. Fortunately, domestic league clashes should be avoided, as Major League Soccer switches to a European-style calendar from 2027-28, ending campaigns in late May. The tournament extends a remarkable run of major events in the US, following the 2025 Club World Cup, the 2026 World Cup, and a joint bid with Mexico, Jamaica and Costa Rica for the 2031 Women's World Cup. Formal confirmation awaits confederation decision Formal confirmation of the 2028 hosts is expected shortly, though a CONMEBOL press officer noted no official statement had yet been received and CONCACAF declined to comment. Meanwhile, the CONMEBOL council met on Friday to reiterate its backing for FIFA president Gianni Infantino ahead of upcoming elections. Next week will also see the joint 2031 Women's World Cup hosting bid officially confirmed.

item.title: Macau GP: Rashid Al Dhaheri defeats Mattia Colnaghi to take qualification race win
item.description: Motorsport photo Rashid Al Dhaheri took victory in the Macau Grand Prix qualification race after jumping polesitter Alex Ninovic at the start and resisting a final-lap attack from Mattia Colnaghi. Rodin racer Ninovic had set the pace during a heavily disrupted opening qualifying session on Thursday that featured five red flags, before Friday's Q2 was rain-affected, but the Australian did not make a great launch from pole and was instantly under pressure from Al Dhaheri. The R-ace GP driver - who finished fourth in the Formula Regional European Championship standings this year - had grabbed the lead before the first turn, while Red Bull Junior Colnaghi demoted Ninovic to third on the run to Lisboa. Colnaghi, who looked rapid in first practice but could not replicate that during the chaotic qualifying, then set about closing the gap to Al Dhaheri. This was 1.1 seconds by the end of the first tour and continued to fluctuate between just below and just over a second for much of the contest. But Colnaghi suddenly closed to within half a second on the penultimate tour and mounted an attack into Lisboa for the final time but was never able to draw alongside his rival. MP Motorsport competitor Colnaghi therefore had to settle for a front-row start for Sunday's main race, finishing just 0.251s behind across the line. Mattia Colnaghi Mattia Colnaghi Ninovic drifted away from the lead duo to end up 3s back from Al Dhaheri but last year's GB3 champion was never under pressure for third, while Pinnacle Motorsport driver Enzo Deligny was fourth. Williams junior Kean Nakamura-Berta was fifth for much of the race but was passed by Indy NXT frontrunner Tymek Kucharczyk in the closing stages. For all the drama during qualifying, the race was relatively incident-free with the only significant clash coming on the third lap when Taito Kato tagged Kabir Anurag out of Lisboa, which damaged the suspension on the latter's RPM machine. Although this forced Anurag to stop on track, his car was quickly cleared without need for a caution. Also in strife was Sebastian Wheldon, who pulled into the pits at mid-distance having struggled at the wheel of a new chassis after his original car split in two pieces following a crash in the Esses that caused one of the multiple qualifying stoppages. item.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
item.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. item.title: 2027: INEC REC seeks traditional rulers’ support for peaceful, secure elections in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Benue State, Mallam Aminu Idris, has called on traditional rulers in the state to promote a peaceful and secure environment before and during the 2027 general elections. Idris made the appeal during a courtesy visit to the Tor Tiv and Chairman of the Benue State Council of Traditional Rulers, His Royal Majesty, Orcivirigh Prof. James Ayatse, on Friday, November 20, 2026, as part of the Commission’s stakeholder engagement ahead of the elections. The REC also solicited the support of the traditional institution in encouraging eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and strengthening collaboration with INEC to ensure successful conduct of the forthcoming polls. According to a statement by the Public Affairs Officer of INEC in Benue State, Mrs. Peace Ogoyi, Idris described the visit as a vital step in the Commission’s preparations for the 2027 elections. “He solicited the intervention and support of the royal father in three key areas: encouraging the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), promoting a peaceful and secure environment before and during the elections, and providing further support to the Commission through sustained collaboration.” Responding, the Tor Tiv welcomed the REC and his delegation, expressing appreciation for the visit and acknowledging the important role of traditional rulers in ensuring a conducive environment for electoral activities. He noted that “traditional rulers, as fathers of the state, have a responsibility to receive electoral officials and ensure their safety and provision of a peaceful working environment. Drawing from his experience in previous elections, including his service in various ad hoc capacities and as a State Returning Officer, Ayatse acknowledged the enormous responsibilities confronting the Commission. He said the Traditional Council had consistently advocated peaceful political campaigns and a level playing field for all political parties. The monarch further disclosed that traditional and religious leaders had organised prayers for peaceful elections and maintained constructive engagements with security agencies to strengthen peace and security across the state. He assured the REC that the Council would continue to collaborate with relevant stakeholders to identify and address electoral security flashpoints ahead of the elections. On the credibility of the electoral process, the Tor Tiv emphasised the need for INEC to uphold the will of the people, urging the Commission’s personnel to discharge their duties with neutrality, fairness and professionalism. He also pledged the continued support of the “Benue State Council of Traditional Rulers towards the successful conduct of the 2027 general elections.” On PVC collection, Prof Ayatse called for “stronger collaboration between Electoral Officers and traditional and religious leaders to intensify public sensit

item.title: Obi best hope for Nigerians, NDC chairman Cleopas declares
item.description: …Says 2027 poll must be referendum on Tinubu’s performance By Emem Idio, Yenagoa The National Chairman of the Nigeria Democratic Congress ,NDC, Senator Moses Cleopas, has described the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, as the best hope for Nigerians, urging the electorate to vote out the President Bola Tinubu-led administration in the 2027 general election. Cleopas said the country could not afford another four years under an administration that, in his assessment, had failed to address the worsening economic hardship, insecurity and rising cost of living. He described the 2027 presidential election as an opportunity for Nigerians to determine the future direction of the country and hold the incumbent government accountable for its performance. The former senator representing Bayelsa Central made the remarks on Friday in Yenagoa during a celebration marking his 57th birthday. He said the election should serve as a referendum on the Tinubu administration, arguing that a second-term mandate must be earned through demonstrable performance rather than political sentiment. “Second-term election is a referendum. It is standing on the leg of your previous performance. If you have done well, they give you another mandate. If you have not done well, they ask you to go home,” he said. Cleopas said the impact of the economic crisis was being felt by families across the country, including his own, citing complaints from his wife and children about the rising cost of household upkeep and education. He urged voters to assess the presidential candidates on the basis of competence, track record and their capacity to address the country’s problems, rather than party loyalty, religious considerations or financial inducements. The NDC chairman expressed confidence that Obi would win the 2027 presidential election, insisting that his candidacy offered Nigerians a credible alternative to the present administration. On insecurity, Cleopas condemned the persistent killings and abductions across the country, particularly attacks involving schoolchildren, accusing the government of failing in its fundamental responsibility to protect lives and property. Recounting his experience in the Senate, he said lawmakers from different parts of northern Nigeria frequently reported killings in their constituencies, including the deaths of women and children. He argued that insecurity should concern every Nigerian, irrespective of where attacks occurred, warning against the tendency to treat violence as a distant problem until it reaches one’s community. Ahead of the 2027 elections, Cleopas accused some politicians of deploying money and public resources to weaken opposition parties and influence voters. He specifically criticised an alleged plan by a political figure in Bayelsa to offer N50,000 per vote, describing the proposal as an affront to the electorate. item.title: NASA Mars rover and orbiter suffer glitches
item.description: It's been a bad few weeks for technology on and off the planet, as NASA reported problems with its Perseverance Mars rover and Odyssey orbiter this week. For Perseverance, the problem seems to be a relatively straightforward communications issue that has paused science operations because of low data rates. The Odyssey orbiter, however, is facing an issue that could end the mission. The 2001 Mars Odyssey reached orbit around Mars in October 2001 to search for evidence of water and ice on the surface. The mission was supposed to last two and a half years, but the spacecraft's operations have been extended for a quarter of a century. In that time, it has had its fair share of ups and downs, including the failure of one of its four reaction wheels in 2013. Three reaction wheels are needed to orient the spacecraft; otherwise, it must fall back to its hydrazine thrusters. Earlier in November, between the 4th and 6th, Odyssey dropped into safe mode, which engineers determined was caused by one of the remaining reaction wheels stopping spinning. Science data stopped flowing as the team worked to recover the component; the good news was that the wheel moved when commanded. The bad news is that if the thrusters need to be used, only a few months of fuel remain. More bad news is that the spacecraft is part of NASA's Mars Relay Network, and was responsible for sending back the first post-landing images from the Phoenix lander and the Spirit, Opportunity, and Curiosity rovers. Its loss (should it come to that) would therefore be keenly felt. In the event the orbiter is indeed approaching the end of the road, the European Space Agency's Mars Express (MEX) and Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO) could pick up some of the load although, as a former ESA insider put it: "MEX is a science mission that can do relay where TGO is a relay mission that also does science." According to NASA, TGO already sends the most relay data from Mars to Earth. The challenge facing the Perseverance trundlebot is one of communication. On October 30, the rover's main computer detected problems with the primary radio (a series of "heartbeats" from the device did not arrive as expected) and automatically switched to a redundant backup, placing itself in a protective safe mode. So far, so expected. Engineers brought the rover back from safe mode, analyzed the data, and made an unpleasant discovery. The backup radio was not performing as it should – it was operating at approximately half of its expected power output. Both radios were therefore deemed inoperable – at least until the team has got to the bottom of the issues – and the rover has used X-band communications over its high-gain antenna to talk to Earth ever since. The problem here is that the connection provides a significantly lower data rate, meaning science and instrument operations are on hold. Engineers are working first to return the backup radio to operational status, then to address the primary. ®

EFCC case: ‘I’m most vilified; I shall be vindicated’– Yahaya Bello
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Former Kogi State Governor Yahaya Bello has described himself as “the most transparent and the most vilified,” saying he expects to be vindicated over corruption allegations against him. Bello spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, saying he would not comment on the EFCC case in detail because it was before the courts. He said Kogi State’s budgets, audited accounts, and records of performance were available online and challenged journalists and others to examine them and ask questions under the Freedom of Information Act. “I’d rather decline to make a comment about EFCC on national television because we’re in court. However, from inception till date, all of our financials and budgets and the performance on the ground are online. We have our eight years’ budget, eight years’ final account, which we call an audited account, and the performance on the ground; we have them online,” he said. Bello said he had experience managing public resources before becoming governor and was already financially established. He said he granted local governments financial autonomy after taking office and left the allegations for the courts to determine. “I was never; I never assumed office as a poor man. I’m a man of my means before I assumed the office. God blessed me in my early age, and my children have been schooling in high-profile schools, both in Abuja and abroad. In any case, I don’t think I was a governor that time. The rest, I’ll leave it for them to prove it in court,” he said. He added, “I am the most transparent and the most vilified. I’m the most transparent. I’m the most vilified. But at the end of the day, I shall be vindicated.” Bello also said he had no regrets about his time as governor and accepted responsibility for what happened during his tenure, adding: “I gave my best.” The EFCC is prosecuting Bello in two separate cases relating to alleged financial misconduct during his 2016–2024 governorship tenure. item.title: 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised after drinking alcohol
item.description: At least 11 people have died and more than 180 have been hospitalised after drinking suspected tainted alcohol in India’s northeastern state of Manipur. The victims fell ill after consuming the liquor, Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh said in a statement on Friday. “Over 180 patients have been admitted in the two hospitals so far, while the death toll has reached 11 in the last 48 hours,” the statement said. He also ordered an enquiry into the incident, saying those responsible would be arrested and punished. Deaths from illicit or adulterated alcohol are regularly reported in India, where cheap liquor sold outside regulated channels can contain methanol, a highly toxic industrial chemical. In May, at least 15 people died after drinking methanol-laced illicit liquor in Pune and neighbouring Pimpri-Chinchwad in the western state of Maharashtra. In August, 13 people died and more than 60 were affected after consuming methanol-tainted liquor in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar district, according to local media reports. Such liquor is widely consumed across India, where a bottle is sometimes sold for less than a dollar. If ingested, methanol can cause blindness, liver damage and death in larger concentrations. Vanguard News The post 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised after drinking alcohol appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Four die, 24 rescued as Bayelsa burial boat capsizes
item.description: Four persons, including two children, have died after a boat conveying passengers to a burial ceremony capsized in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State on Friday. Twenty-four other passengers were rescued following the incident, which occurred at about 11am while the boat was travelling from Ayama community to Ukubie. The Bayelsa State Police Command said preliminary findings indicated that the boat developed a mechanical fault while navigating the waterways. The police spokesperson, Musa Mohammed, disclosed this in a statement on Friday, alleging that some passengers had urged the operator to steer towards the riverbank after the fault developed, but he declined and continued the journey before the boat capsized. Mohammed said the bodies of two adults and two children had been recovered and deposited at the mortuary of the Federal Medical Centre, Yenagoa. He said 24 survivors were rescued, with 19 taken to Ayama Clinic, while five others who sustained injuries were transferred to Family Care Hospital in Yenagoa for treatment. The police spokesperson disclosed that the boat operator, identified only as Omovie, had fled the scene, while the boat manager, identified as MV Bina, had been taken into custody for investigation. He added that the police marine section had been deployed to reinforce search and rescue operations, while the Divisional Police Officer in Oporoma was coordinating efforts with local divers and other emergency responders. Mohammed said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the tragedy, assuring that search and rescue operations would continue until everyone on board had been accounted for. item.title: UNICEF raises alarm over 624,000 out-of-school children
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) has raised concerns over the high number of out-of-school children in Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara states, disclosing that about 624,000 children have been identified as being outside the classroom across the three states. The organisation said although about 68,000 children had benefited from interventions to return them to school, the scale of the challenge required urgent government action, increased investment and stronger community mobilisation. UNICEF’s Chief of Field Office in Sokoto, Dr Michael Juma, made this known at a media briefing organised by the organisation’s Sokoto Field Office as part of activities marking the 2026 World Children’s Day. He called for coordinated action by governments, media organisations, traditional institutions, religious leaders and community stakeholders to address challenges confronting children in the region. Juma urged journalists across the three states to intensify public enlightenment, investigative reporting and advocacy to promote children’s rights, strengthen government accountability and ensure access to education, healthcare, nutrition and other essential services. Describing the media as a critical partner in advancing children’s rights, he said journalists must go beyond reporting events to exposing gaps in service delivery and holding relevant authorities accountable. “The media are important duty-bearers in advancing children’s rights. Journalists must provide balanced coverage that highlights development achievements while drawing attention to persistent gaps affecting the wellbeing of children,” he said. He reaffirmed UNICEF’s commitment to strengthening collaboration with the governments of Sokoto, Kebbi and Zamfara, development partners, traditional and religious leaders, and grassroots organisations to guarantee children access to quality and inclusive education, healthcare, adequate nutrition, safe drinking water and social protection. Providing an account of interventions undertaken through UNICEF’s partnerships with the three state governments, Juma disclosed that approximately 98,000 children had benefited from the Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) programme, designed to improve foundational literacy and numeracy. He said the organisation was also supporting teacher professional development, provision of instructional materials, accelerated basic education, integrated Qur’anic education and innovative learning opportunities, including radio-based education and the Nigeria Learning Passport. According to him, the interventions are particularly targeted at children affected by insecurity, displacement and other emergencies. On healthcare and immunisation, Juma disclosed that approximately 7.8 million children across the three states had been reached through measles-rubella vaccination, while more than five million children were vaccinated during the last concluded polio immunisation campaign. item.title: ‘Issakaba Returns’ grosses N47.8m in opening weekend, sets new record for Nollywood action thriller
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku The highly anticipated Nollywood classic, “Issakaba Returns” stormed the domestic box office, recording a spectacular opening weekend gross of N47.8 million to become the highest-grossing debut ever for an action thriller. The film, directed by popular filmmaker and producer, Lancelot Oduwa Imasuen, premiered last Wednesday at Silverbird Cinemas, Victoria Island, Lagos. Celebrating the feat, Lancelot, fondly called D’Guvnor, thanked everyone who showed up, bought tickets, filled the cinemas and embraced “Issakaba Returns” with so much love. “To everyone who has supported this journey, shared the excitement, spread the word and made the opening weekend this remarkable, I do not take your love for granted. “This is more than numbers. It is a testament to the love, nostalgia and connection you all have with this story. “N47.8 million opening weekend gross, and this is only the beginning! “Thank you for believing in us. Thank you for showing up. The love has been organic, and we feel every bit of it,” Lancelot said. The premiere of “Issakaba Returns” was spectacular and memorable. The evening exploded into war songs, cultural dance and gyration as the film began its cinema run. Long before the lights went down inside the cinema hall, the carnival had already begun outside. Drummers, dancers and chanting fans set the mood, recreating the fearless spirit of the Issakaba Boys who, 25 years ago, stood against evil in the South-East. For the lead character, Sam Dede, the return is more than nostalgia. It is a message. Speaking at the premiere, he said the evils the Issakaba Boys fought a quarter of a century ago, kidnapping, money rituals, human trafficking are still ravaging society today. First released in 2001 and inspired by real-life vigilante movements, the original “Issakaba” became a cultural phenomenon. item.title: Davido and Chioma: The love story continues
item.description: By Benjamin Njoku Afrobeats superstar Davido is known for flaunting his wife, Chioma Adeleke, on social media, displaying public affection and storming international show venues in her company. It is no surprise, therefore, that the three-time Grammy nominee has taken their romance to the studio, borrowing a leaf from the likes of Adekunle Gold and Simi, Banky W and Adesuwa Etomi, as well as Beyoncé and Jay-Z, who have all turned their love stories into music. For Davido, Chioma has never just been his wife. She has been his muse from the very beginning. Their love story in music started in 2018 with ‘Assurance’, the birthday gift Davido dedicated to Chioma when they were still dating. Chioma starred in the video, and the song became one of the most iconic love anthems in Afrobeats history. She returned in 2020 for ‘1 Milli’, whose wedding-themed video further celebrated their relationship. Nearly eight years after ‘Assurance’, ‘Already Falling’ brings that story full circle, from young lovers to husband and wife. The song, the eighth track on Davido’s sixth studio album, “ORIADÉ”, was released on July 31, 2026. It blends English, Yoruba and Nigerian Pidgin, and reimagines Elvis Presley’s timeless classic ‘Can’t Help Falling in Love’ through an Afrobeats lens with background vocals by Peruzz The official video, released on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, stars Chioma as his leading lady once again. Directed by Meji Alabi, who also directed ‘Assurance, the video was filmed at the historic Château de Chanteloup, the estate of French cognac house Maison Martell in Cognac, France. It blends French elegance with Nigerian style, with Davido arriving in a horse-drawn carriage, serenading Chioma in grand interiors, and later recreating a proposal scene by a lake at dusk, where he goes down on one knee to present her with a ring. Though the couple wedded in a lavish Lagos ceremony in June 2024, the proposal scene is a cinematic metaphor for renewed commitment, not a new engagement. Davido announced the release himself with the caption: “Already Falling. From us to you. Enjoy.” Like other music stars, Davido is proving that a real-life love story can become a powerful artistic brand. For fans, ‘Already Falling’ is more than a music video. It is a continuation of a story they have followed since 2018 ; from young lovers, to husband and wife, to parents, told in Davido’s most personal songs. And with Chioma by his side in the studio, on screen, and on tour, including their recent high-profile trip to Tanzania with Diamond Platnumz, the couple shows no signs of slowing down. item.title: Soludo approves N50,000 December bonus for Anambra workers
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has approved a N50,000 December bonus for civil servants in the state, with the payment expected to reflect in their December 2026 salaries. The governor announced the bonus during the 2026 Civil Service Day celebration held at the Jerome Udoji State Secretariat Complex in Awka, where he also approved measures to improve the working environment and productivity of civil servants. Soludo acknowledged the economic challenges facing workers, admitting that their current salaries were inadequate amid prevailing economic conditions. He, however, assured the workers that his administration would only make financial commitments it could realistically fulfil. “I understand the situation and economic conditions, that we need to be able to do something. The pay that we have all over is not enough; I clearly understand it. “But there is one thing I also want to tell you, and that is I don’t play to the wind. Before we get into a commitment, we make sure that it is something that we will always honour,” he said. Addressing comparisons between Anambra’s salary structure and those of other states, the governor urged civil servants to consider the different revenue bases and economic capacities of state governments before making such assessments. He stressed that sustainable governance and responsible financial management, rather than unfulfilled promises, remained the guiding principles of his administration. Soludo also expressed appreciation to the workers for their support during last year’s governorship election, saying he was pleased that public servants overwhelmingly voted for his administration in recognition of its developmental efforts. Responding to three major requests presented by the workers at the event, the governor immediately directed the rehabilitation of roads within the secretariat complex, approved the establishment of an Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Centre and authorised the pruning of overgrown trees across the premises. Earlier, the Anambra State Head of Service, Barr. Ngozi Iwouno, commended Soludo for restoring security and normalcy across the state. She said civil servants could now attend work regularly without fear, noting that the disruption previously caused by Monday sit-at-home orders had been overcome. Iwouno said the improved security situation had restored confidence among workers and enabled them to discharge their duties more consistently. item.title: ‘The doom of humanity’: will the quest to make robotic hands render us obsolete?
item.description: The one thing stopping AI taking over the world – or at least everyone’s jobs? Dexterity. Human hands are anatomical marvels that engineers have struggled for years to replicate. Experts are racing to change that Just outside Luton, in an Amazon warehouse the size of four football pitches, yellow shelving units pirouette in a digitally choreographed dance. Tubs containing a Lego Spider-Man kit, followed by dishwasher tablets, followed by a pouch of muscle building protein powder whiz along conveyor belts, until they arrive at a human being tasked with stacking the shelving unit that has come to a stop in front of their workstation. This, Amazon says, is the “symphony of people and technology” to which the retail giant owes its success. Following a barrage of negative publicity about working practices, Amazon began to open up its fulfilment centres to carefully controlled free public tours a decade ago. Our guide tells us about the competitive rates of pay Amazon workers receive, their pensions, dental cover and options for flexible working. Her delivery is somewhat robotic. Continue reading...

item.title: Passengers fear proposed biometric checks may cause chaos at domestic airports
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Federal Government’s proposed mandatory biometric checks for domestic air passengers from January 1, 2027, have come under scrutiny less than five days after the plan was announced, with passengers and industry observers warning that the policy could make air travel more difficult. They insisted that the plan appeared rushed and had not been properly thought through, particularly as the festive travel season would still be ongoing when the policy takes effect. They also feared that its implementation could trigger a repeat of the chaos that followed the introduction of the Go Cashless payment system, which caused hours of gridlock at airports in Lagos and Abuja. In March, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, introduced an electronic payment system known as Go Cashless at the toll gate of two of the country’s busiest airports. Its rollout left passengers travelling through the airports in Lagos and Abuja stranded for hours, triggering massive gridlock, missed flights and widespread frustration. While some travellers abandoned their vehicles at airport entrances after encountering difficulties completing payments, others said they missed scheduled flights after spending hours trying to gain access to the airports. The disruption prompted President Bola Tinubu to order the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr Festus Keyamo, to announce a suspension of the system on the fourth day of its implementation. With the busy Yuletide travel period extending into January, passengers and industry observers fear that a similar situation could unfold at the Lagos airport, the country’s busiest, especially as Keyamo has given domestic airlines until December 31, 2026, to integrate their operations with the system that will facilitate the biometric checks. Keyamo warned that airlines that fail to comply with the directive would not be allowed to board passengers from January 1, 2027. Known as the Airport Passenger Verification System, v-PASS, the biometric identity verification system is linked to the National Identification Number, NIN, of Nigerians. It is designed exclusively for domestic flights, with all passengers required to provide their NIN during check-in. Passengers are also expected to pay additional charges for the service. Speaking during the unveiling of the system at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, Keyamo said: “I am giving the airlines till the end of December. I repeat it. From the 1st of January, no airline will be allowed to board their passengers if they don’t key into the v-PASS.” X-raying v-PASS Approved by the Federal Executive Council, FEC, v-PASS is a private-sector investment aimed at modernising airport operations through private-sector participation. item.description: By Dayo Johnson, AKURE The Ondo State Government has released an eight-day programme of burial activities for the late elder statesman and Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, CFR, with his funeral service and interment scheduled for Thursday, December 17, 2026. The programme, signed by the Chairman and Secretary of the State Burial Committee, Dr Kayode Ajulo and Apostle Eniola Olushola, Esq, respectively, shows that the ceremonies will begin on Sunday, December 13, with a cultural heritage day in honour of the deceased, who was born on May 11, 1926 and died on October 20, 2026. The opening ceremony, scheduled for 12 noon, will feature a showcase of Ondo State’s cultural heritage at the Dr Olusegun Mimiko International Centre for Culture and Events (The Dome), Akure. A commendation service will hold at Anglican Grammar School, Iju-Itaogbolu, at 9.00 am on Monday, December 14, followed by a novelty football match in Fasoranti’s honour at the Akure Township Stadium. The football fixtures will see Anglican Grammar School, Iju-Itaogbolu, take on St Frances, Akure, at 2.00 pm, while Akure High School will face Ondo Boys High School at 4.00 pm. Activities on Tuesday, December 15, will feature a symposium, national tribute and academic award at The Dome, Akure. The symposium, themed “A Selfless Cradle Light That The Yoruba Race Can’t Forget In A Hurry”, will be organised by Afenifere, the DAWN Commission and the Ondo State Government. It is scheduled for 10.00 am and will be followed by a national tribute and academic award. A lying-in-state and Christian wake-keep will take place at the deceased’s country home, Omolere Close, Akure, at 4.00 pm on Wednesday, December 16. The funeral service will hold at St David’s Anglican Cathedral, Ijomu, Akure, at 10.00 am prompt on Thursday, December 17, with interment to follow immediately at the church cemetery. A reception and entertainment of guests will subsequently hold at designated venues for the different categories of guests. The programme will continue on Friday, December 18, with a thanksgiving service at Akure Central Mosque at 1.00 pm, while Saturday, December 19, has been set aside for family visits to Baba’s residence. The final activity, an outing and thanksgiving service, will hold at St David’s Anglican Cathedral, Ijomu, Akure, at 10.00 am prompt on Sunday, December 20. The post Pa Fasoranti for burial Dec 17; Ondo govt unveils 8-day programme appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigerian researcher Babsalaam proposes framework to strengthen multi-cloud resilience
item.description: By Ayo Taiwo As organisations increasingly rely on cloud technology to deliver essential services, Nigerian researcher Adebimpe Babsalaam has proposed an integrated framework to help businesses prevent service disruptions and improve data recovery across multiple cloud platforms. In a research paper titled “Designing Resilient Multi-Cloud Architectures Through Fault-Tolerant Systems, Automated Failover and Disaster Recovery Optimisation,” published in the International Journal of Computer and Artificial Intelligence , Babsalaam examines how organisations can maintain digital services when cloud infrastructure, networks or entire regions experience failures. She argues that using multiple cloud providers does not automatically guarantee protection against disruptions, as different platforms may still share critical network, storage and database dependencies. The proposed framework combines fault-tolerant infrastructure, predictive failure analysis, automated failover and disaster recovery to minimise downtime and protect critical business operations. According to the study, the architecture distributes applications, databases and storage services across multiple cloud providers and geographically separated regions. It also uses monitoring systems to detect infrastructure problems and redirect users to functioning services. Babsalaam identifies two deployment approaches: active-active, where multiple cloud environments handle traffic simultaneously, and active-passive, where a secondary environment remains on standby until the primary system fails. The study recommends selecting an approach based on the importance of the application, performance requirements and acceptable downtime. It also proposes using predictive models, including machine learning techniques, to identify warning signs of potential infrastructure failures before they develop into major outages. However, Babsalaam notes that predicting a failure is not enough if recovery systems are not properly prepared. A system may successfully forecast an outage but still leave users without access to services if backup infrastructure is unavailable, replicated data is outdated or recovery processes are too slow. The framework therefore combines predictive warnings with automated responses, including activating standby infrastructure, redirecting network traffic and restoring data. It also recommends safeguards to prevent unnecessary failovers, conflicting database records and situations where multiple systems mistakenly operate as the primary service. The research further highlights the importance of recovery time objectives (RTO), which define how quickly services must be restored, and recovery point objectives (RPO), which determine how much data an organisation can afford to lose. According to the paper, organisations must balance these requirements against infrastructure costs, network performance and data replication needs. item.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for US Space Force from California
item.description: null SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force tonight (Nov. 20), sending a mystery payload to orbit from California's central coast. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:20 p.m. EST (8:20 p.m. local California time; 0420 GMT on Nov. 21), on a Space Force mission called USSF-317. The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth about 8.5 minutes later, touching down in the Pacific Ocean atop the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You." It was the 11th launch and landing for this booster, which is designated B1100. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship after launching the USSF-317 mission. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX ended its launch webcast just after that touchdown, so we didn't get to see the Falcon 9's upper stage power its way to orbit. USSF-317 is a classified mission, so we don't know what the upper stage is carrying or where exactly it's headed. However, some experts think that USSF-317 may be hauling a batch of SpaceX's Starshield satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Space Force's Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio, which helps the military keep tabs on potential targets around the world. Previous Booster 1100 missions NROL-105 | USSF-385 | 8 Starlink missions USSF-317 was the 121st Falcon 9 launch of 2026 and the third mission that SpaceX has launched for the Space Force so far in November. The vast majority of this year's Falcon 9 missions — about 70% of them — have been devoted to building out SpaceX's Starlink LEO internet constellation, which currently consists of more than 11,000 satellites. The Falcon 9 has been putting up incredible numbers lately — it flew a whopping 165 times in 2025 , for example — but the workhorse rocket is on its way out . SpaceX plans to retire both it and the Falcon Heavy in favor of its fully reusable Starship megarocket, which deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 satellites on its most recent two test flights .

item.title: ‘Leadership should not depend on luck’ – Okoroama on preparing technical experts for management
item.description: By Ayo Taiwo Nigerian engineering leader and business psychology specialist James Okoroama has introduced a leadership development model aimed at helping technically accomplished professionals navigate the challenges of transitioning into management. Okoroama presented his N-Curve Leadership Model at the 2026 Annual Conference of the Society for Maintenance & Reliability Professionals (SMRP), held in Raleigh, North Carolina, from September 28 to October 1. His presentation, titled “Leading Through the Dip: From Technical Expertise to Maintenance and Reliability Engineering Leadership Mastery,” examined why professionals who excel in technical roles sometimes struggle when promoted into leadership positions. The N-Curve model describes a transition in which employees may experience a temporary decline in confidence, effectiveness or perceived competence as they move from technical responsibilities to managing people and organisational performance. According to Okoroama, technical expertise does not automatically translate into the ability to lead teams, delegate responsibilities and develop other professionals. “We promote people for being the best fixer in the room, then ask them to stop fixing,” Okoroama said. “Of course there is a dip. The mistake is pretending it will not happen.” The model outlines a progression from technical mastery through promotion and a potential leadership dip, followed by adaptation and eventual leadership proficiency. Okoroama said that the transition requires professionals to move beyond individual technical achievements and develop skills in delegation, communication, coaching, conflict resolution and performance management. He introduced the model in a December 2025 research paper alongside a complementary framework known as the Situational Reliability Leadership Matrix, which proposes tailoring leadership development to individual readiness and organisational demands. His interest in the subject draws partly from his professional journey, which began with technical apprenticeship in Nigeria before progressing through equipment maintenance, reliability engineering, consulting and engineering management. He currently serves as a senior regional reliability engineering and robotics leader at Amazon, where he leads a technical organisation of more than 600 professionals supporting industrial automation and robotics operations. In 2026, he also serves as an RME Engagement and Workforce Development Strategy Partner within Amazon’s North America Customer Fulfillment network. Okoroama holds a Master of Science degree from the University of South Wales, where his studies explored the relationship between human behaviour, organisational performance and leadership. The research has implications for Nigerian organisations across manufacturing, energy, telecommunications and other sectors where technically skilled employees are frequently promoted into supervisory positions without sufficient leadership preparation. item.title: APOD: 2026 November 21 – Voyager’s Neptune
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 21 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Voyager’s Neptune Explanation: Cruising through the outer solar system, the Voyager 2 spacecraft made its closest approach to Neptune on August 25, 1989, the only spacecraft to visit the most distant ice giant planet . Based on the images recorded during its close encounter and in the following days, this inspired composited scene covers the dim outer planet, largest moon Triton , and faint system of rings. From just beyond Neptune’s orbit, the interplanetary perspective looks back toward the Sun, capturing the planet and Triton as thin sunlit crescents . Cirrus clouds and a dark band circle Neptune’s south polar region, with a cloudy vortex above the pole itself . Parts of the very faint ring system along with the three bright ring arcs were first imaged by Voyager during the fly-by, though the faintest segments are modeled in this composited picture. Spanning 7.5 degrees, the background starfield is composed from sky survey data centered on the constellation Camelopardalis, corresponding to the outbound Voyager’s view of the magnificent Neptunian system . Still cruising in 2026, the Voyager 2 spacecraft is now in interstellar space . item.title: Amazon's split personality: AWS embraces bot commerce while main site enforces bans
item.description: Amazon is of two minds when it comes to automated purchasing. The ecommerce giant has been busy banning AI shopping agents from accessing its website. Meanwhile, AWS Marketplace has opened its door to bot-based buying. "Buying software and data through AWS Marketplace just got easier, for you and for the AI agents working alongside you," said Mya Papolu, product marketing manager for AWS Marketplace and Partner Services at Amazon Web Services, in a blog post this week. "For re:Invent 2026, we’re launching capabilities designed to reduce friction across the buying journey." For a company that has blocked bots from Google, Meta, and OpenAI, and sued Perplexity to keep its AI-encumbered Comet browser away, the openness of AWS Marketplace to agentic commerce invites questions. We asked Amazon to explain but we've not heard back. AWS Marketplace is allowing AI agents to scour its site and buy some cloud software products using the x402 agentic payment protocol , which is supported by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments. Introduced by Coinbase and Cloudflare , x402 got handed over to the Linux Foundation earlier this year, and now has support from a variety of tech platforms, including AWS, Google, Stripe, and various blockchain networks. About a week ago, Brave Software announced support for x402 payments through its search API. AWS requires sellers to register with AWS Marketplace and to integrate the AWS Marketplace x402 SDK to enable agentic product purchases. Transactions settle in USD through AWS billing so existing spending controls can be applied. And now, customers in the US can buy some AWS Marketplace software without an AWS account; instead they're asked to provide an email or social media login, and a credit card. While AWS Marketplace today lists mainly familiar software categories (Business Applications, Data & Analytics, DevOps, Infrastructure Software, and so on), AWS has a broader product inventory in mind. Beyond software and APIs, the biz sees a future in selling content and data. Papolu announced that AWS is now selling " data as a service ." "Data providers can list their offerings in AWS Marketplace, making commercial data accessible to both human teams and the agents working alongside them via the AWS Marketplace website, APIs, and MCP server," she said. This includes services like Moody's Credit MCP server for financial research; Reuters Geopolitical News for AI-structured reporting; US Building Permits, Contractors & Residents Data from Shovels; and US-EN Multi-Speaker Conversational Acoustic Corpus from Uber AI Solutions. In canned remarks provided to AWS, Nandhan Puppala, general manager at Uber AI Solutions, said that data quality and readiness can help advance AI products. Agent mode for AWS Marketplace has been available for about a year as a way to query the market via prompt. That's being expanded to allow deeper queries about seller security and project requirements. Science fiction writer William Gibson's oft-cited line

PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
item.description: On Thursday, PHP version 8.6 was released on its usual yearly schedule, popping up as if the web scripting language hadn’t been under intense scrutiny this past month. For those who missed it: a swarm of unearthed vulnerabilities has plagued PHP since October, allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash PHP workers or execute arbitrary code on the server. Users of every PHP-based application, including WordPress, Laravel, and Symfony, had to scramble to update their PHP instances. The PHP core development community, along with the PHP Foundation , responded with a coordinated release of patched versions of PHP ( 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and the new 8.6) that closed seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws in one sweep. In addition to patching specific exploitable holes in the PHP engine, the new version of PHP also tamps down some of PHP’s historically liberal configuration settings. Lucky for PHP, and for the rest of us, core developer Jörg Sowa called out these lax settings in June, when he posted a proposal to set more security-friendly defaults. Sowa saw that three configuration settings of PHP’s session extension – Strict Mode, HttpOnly, and SameSite – were designed to boost security but shipped “with defaults that leave applications unnecessarily exposed.” No cookies for impostors In a retrospective posted last month, the PHP Foundation admitted that consensus-driven gridlock had stalled complex fixes for months and vowed to get patches out the door sooner, should the vulnerabilities leak ahead of the agreed-upon deadline . Code-wise, Sowa’s proposal to harden PHP settings was accepted for PHP 8.6. These changes won’t stop the flood of AI-generated CVEs, but at least these holes will be more difficult to exploit. For Strict Mode, PHP will no longer accept uninitialized session IDs that it didn’t create itself. Before, an attacker could just plant a made-up session ID on the victim to gain entry. “The built-in files handler checks whether a session file for that ID exists on disk; because an attacker-planted ID has no corresponding file, a fresh random ID is generated instead,” Sowa wrote. Furthermore, PHP will now, by default, add the HttpOnly flag to its session Set-Cookie header, blocking client-side JavaScript from reading the session ID, which could otherwise be stolen to masquerade as the user. Believe it or not, any script on the page could read it before. Finally, the server will withhold session cookies on cross-site POST requests, as well as for subrequests and iframes. “Without it, a forged form or link on an attacker-controlled site can trigger authenticated requests using the victim’s session,” Sowa wrote. Going forward, cookies will only be sent on same-site requests and top-level GET navigations, such as clicking a normal link. Collectively, these changes should thwart session hijacking and cross-site request forgeries. They won’t stop remote code execution hacks, though they will make it a lot more difficult for

item.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
item.description: Visa and Mastercard customer info leaked by the data thieves and extortionists who claim to have stolen it from the financial giants doesn’t include card numbers, passwords, or home addresses. On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand. Researchers at SOCRadar, a threat-intelligence firm that has been tracking n0n since it emerged in September, have parsed all 14 files in the n0n’s published Visa and Mastercard archives, and told us that the files don’t contain any financial details belonging to banking customers. “We found no card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, passwords, dates of birth, or home addresses in any file,” Ensar Seker, SOCRadar chief information security officer, told The Register . “Visa's statement that no card numbers were affected matches our scan.” Mastercard previously said that stolen data included a “limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information” from a subset of cardholders in a benefits program. According to SOCRadar’s analysis, the leaked files do contain mobile numbers, Bank Identification Number (BIN) prefixes, and dated airline, hotel, and restaurant bookings. So while the data doesn’t include card or account numbers that crooks could use to drain customers' bank accounts or rack up massive credit card bills, “that detail is what a fraudster needs to pose as a concierge desk or a bank,” in an email or voice-phishing social engineering attack, Seker said. It’s also worth noting that the published files only represent about 0.4 percent of the data n0n claims to have hoovered up in the breach: about 4.3 GB and 1.9 million marketing events. “So a further release is possible,” according to Seker. Plus, both datasets come from the same upstream provider, we’re told. They use the same 27-column booking layout, placeholder text, and CRM ID format, Seker said, noting that the most recent record in each stops 69 seconds apart on Oct 26. “This looks like two card programs run on one provider's platform,” he said. “The pattern looks like a batch copy from a marketing and reporting store.” Customer data has left the building The security shop hasn’t analyzed the Chase customer data that n0n also claimed to have published. All three financial firms attributed the compromises to a third-party provider, and while nothing in the stolen files name the vendor, the timing matches up with a Qubole supply-chain campaign disclosed earlier this month by Wiz, working with Google's Mandiant incident responders and AI data security company Sentra.
